whats-one-trait-every-standout-linkedin-.excerpt: The one trait every standout LinkedIn brand will share in 2026 is TRUST. More specifically, it is the ability to consistently build emotional trust through a clear voice, human presence,…
whats-one-trait-every-standout-linkedin-.body:
The one trait every standout LinkedIn brand will share in 2026 is **TRUST**. More specifically, it is the ability to consistently build emotional trust through a clear voice, human presence, and aligned content, even as automation and AI become more common.

I came across a statistic that reinforced why this matters, only [28% of Americans](https://news.gallup.com/poll/695762/trust-media-new-low.aspx)say they trust the media today. While that figure is often tied to news, the impact stretches across the entire digital landscape. It affects how people consume content, evaluate credibility, and decide which voices are worth listening to online.

As a result, people are no longer choosing content based on visibility alone, they are choosing based on belief. In a [recent episode](https://youtu.be/bhfxDd44_rQ?si=gg6N0rI_ZmzTivNF)of _YOUmanize™ Your Brand_, Rachel and I had an unscripted conversation about trust, alignment, and where personal branding quietly goes wrong as we head into 2026. It wasn’t tactical. It was about how trust is built, how misalignment erodes credibility, and why AI is speeding all of that up.

One question stayed with me: would the people closest to you believe what you put online? As automation increases and trust declines, this feels like the question more leaders need to sit with.

## Why Is Trust More Important Than Reach in 2026?

Trust matters more than reach in 2026 because visibility without credibility does not lead to influence or connection. People may see your content, but without trust, it does not stick or lead to action.

On LinkedIn, this shift is already obvious. Content volume is high, but attention is selective. Audiences are overwhelmed by generic messaging and automated posts that lack a clear human presence. What resonates now is content that feels intentional, grounded, and connected to a real person.

> Reach may get you noticed once; trust is what brings people back.

Google’s research on the [Zero Moment of Truth](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQP2zLYmCG8) shows that it takes an average of 11 touchpoints before someone trusts you enough to take action. That means trust is built gradually, through repeated exposure, not through a single post or moment of visibility.

Your LinkedIn content plays a role in those moments, but only when it actually sounds like you and reflects something people can recognize and remember. The difference between posts that disappear and posts that lead to real opportunities is not reach or timing. It’s whether your perspective stays with someone after they scroll past. When your expertise is clear, human, and consistent, it doesn’t just get seen, it gets remembered.

## Is Scaling Content Still a Smart Strategy in 2026?

Scaling content is only effective in 2026 if trust is scaled alongside it. Posting more without strengthening credibility often weakens a brand rather than growing it. Many leaders assume that consistency means frequency, but consistency is really about alignment. When content increases without a clear voice or purpose, it blends into the background. Thoughtful content that reflects a distinct perspective builds authority even at a lower volume. The goal is not to post more, the goal is to show up more clearly.

## How Does AI Impact Personal Branding and Trust?

AI impacts personal branding by increasing efficiency, but it cannot replace authenticity or emotional connection. Used correctly, AI supports your voice, used incorrectly, it flattens it.

I am very open about the fact that I love AI and use it often. It helps with ideation, drafting, and execution. However, AI does not carry lived experience, nuance, or values. When leaders rely on automation without grounding it in who they are, the result is content that feels technically fine but emotionally empty. In a low trust environment, emotional clarity is everything.

## Why Is Trust in Digital Content So Low Right Now?

Trust in digital content is low because confidence in media and online information has steadily declined over time. This has reshaped how people interpret everything they see online. Decades ago, most Americans trusted the news, today, [fewer than 1 in 3 do](https://news.gallup.com/poll/695762/trust-media-new-low.aspx). That erosion of trust has carried over into social platforms and branded content. As a result, credibility is no longer assumed. It must be built intentionally through consistency, transparency, and presence. This is why who you are matters just as much as what you publish.

## What Traits Will Standout LinkedIn Brands Share in 2026?

Standout LinkedIn brands in 2026 will share 3 traits:

👉 Voice ownership

👉 Strategic imperfection

👉 And scalable authenticity

Voice ownership means having a clear perspective and values that guide your content. Strategic imperfection means allowing space for honesty and humanity rather than hiding behind polish. Scalable authenticity means building systems that support your identity instead of diluting it as you grow. Together, these 3 traits create content that feels human, trustworthy, and consistent over time.

## Why Is LinkedIn a Credibility Platform?

LinkedIn is a credibility platform because people use it to decide who they trust professionally. It is no longer just a place to publish content. Audiences are forming opinions long before conversations happen. Your posts, comments, and presence all contribute to how you are perceived. Whether you realize it or not, your content is speaking for you when you are not in the room. This makes clarity and alignment more important than ever.

## Why Does YOUmanize™ Matter in 2026?

YOUmanize™ matters because it helps leaders maintain trust and presence in an increasingly automated digital world. It ensures that content reflects the person behind the brand, not just the output of a system. This approach is not about rejecting AI, it's about leading with intention. YOUmanize™ helps turn visibility into connection and connection into credibility by keeping the human at the center of the strategy.

> In a year where tools are accessible to everyone, your humanity becomes the advantage.

## What Should Leaders Focus on Building Moving Into 2026?

Leaders should focus on building clarity, consistency, and trust rather than chasing reach or frequency. These elements create long-term credibility.

I am open about the[topics](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuablee_leadership-mentalhealth-humanfirst-activity-7414320664293269504-BtXn?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAABJssUBPwl3cL4QsEPk6ovUlOLHvqdIgOA)that matter to me, including AI, leadership, trust, mental health, and building a blended famiLEE while growing a business with my wife and partner, [Rachel Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAAnoqa4BtQLrxYN5DBPVhfx03Z9LQ-eH3yA?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAAnoqa4BtQLrxYN5DBPVhfx03Z9LQ-eH3yA) . That openness is not a tactic, it is alignment. And alignment is what audiences respond to when trust is scarce. The brands that last will not be the loudest, they will be the ones people trust.

## How Can You Build a Trust Led LinkedIn Brand Now?

You build a trust led LinkedIn brand by clarifying your voice and aligning your content with who you are. That is the foundation of everything that works long-term. If this resonated with you, I would genuinely love to hear what you are doing right now to build trust in your leadership and content. And if you are ready to build a LinkedIn presence that reflects who you really are, that is exactly the work we do inside [LinkedIn Brand LaunchPad.](https://standoutauthority.com/brandlaunchpad)

No pressure. No noise. Just a real conversation.

🔵 For leaders who don’t want to play catch up.

🔵 For people who want to lead AI, not fear it.

🔵 For professionals ready to build a personal brand that multiplies their visibility, their voice, and their impact.

We’ve opened up [5 new spots for Q1 2026](https://standoutauthority.com/brandlaunchpad). If you’re ready to stop blending in and finally take control of your narrative, let’s talk. I’ve also put together a [FREE guide](https://standoutauthority.com/3hiddensignals) to help you tap into LinkedIn’s hidden algorithm, the same one elite execs use to get found by the _right_ people (without posting every day).

I’m sharing this recap to give you one simple, clear place to revisit the insights that mattered most and to carry that momentum into 2026 with intention. This year also marked a major milestone: [Rachel B. Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/therachelblee?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAATthuAB-Gy4FMm8KnvDftaFczqyPAUOIsI) and I launched the [YOUmanize™ Your Brand Podcast](https://www.youtube.com/@YOUmanizeYourBrand), a project rooted in everything I believe about showing up fully as yourself online. It’s been a year of growth, alignment, and doubling down on what works: real connection over vanity metrics. It’s also about acknowledging and opening up about the challenges of being a father of 3, a business owner, a leader and a husband.

age-ai-what-makes-people-actually-click-.title: In the Age of AI, What Makes People Actually Click and Care?
age-ai-what-makes-people-actually-click-.excerpt: In the age of AI, people click and care when content feels human, not just optimized. It’s not the polished perfection or keyword density that builds trust; it’s the messy, real,…
age-ai-what-makes-people-actually-click-.body:
In the age of AI, people click and care when content feels _human_, not just optimized. It’s not the polished perfection or keyword density that builds trust; it’s the messy, real, emotionally authentic stories that reflect lived experience. Whether it’s a vulnerable lesson, a behind-the-scenes moment, or a post that sounds like _you_ (not a bot), connection, not automation, is what drives engagement going into 2026. In a world flooded with AI-generated sameness, what stands out is your voice, your truth, and your willingness to show up as you.

### Why Is “Human Made” Content the Advantage You Need in an AI Flooded World?

Human made storytelling helps business leaders and entrepreneurs stand out by building emotional connection, trust, and brand loyalty, without relying on paid media (ads) or perfection. We’re living in an era where content is instant, AI is everywhere, and automation is the default setting. But the faster the tech evolves, the more people are craving something different… something REAL.

That hunger is not just personal connections with the people in our lives, it’s showing up in the way we work. In advertising, on LinkedIn, and even in how search engines rank content. People want to see the human behind the post, not the polished, airbrushed (or AI-brushed) version. Just the real, relatable, “everything went wrong last week” version of you.

In this Dopamine Dose edition, I’m breaking down how to ride this human first wave and why (even as an AI enthusiast) I believe it’s the single most powerful shift you can make for your brand in 2026.

### Why Are Brands Shifting Back to Human-Made Content in 2025?

Brands are shifting back to human made content in 2025 because consumers are suspicious of AI-generated content. That’s why human derived content leads to higher engagement, loyalty, and conversions. What drives people towards brands today is not glossy production or perfect messaging. After a solid few years of AI-driven everything, audiences are tuning out anything that looks like, smells like, or feels like it’s robotic, and leaning into content that feels personal.

And it’s because people don’t want “perfect.” They want honest and relatable. The kind of content that feels like it was made _by_someone who’s _been there_ not by a bot trying to be human. Here’s a few thoughts to keep in mind when you’re planning your content next:

🔵 AI writes for clicks, humans write for connection.

🔵 Human connection is where dopamine lives.

🔵 This is your green light to stop sounding polished and overanalyzing every post you put out.

Just be real, if there’s a small spelling mistake, so what, it shows YOU wrote it. So quit trying to pump the internet with your _perfect ai generated content_, share what’s real to you.

### What Is the Human Algorithm and Why Does It Matter More Than LinkedIn’s?

The Human Algorithm is the emotional decision-making system that drives engagement, trust, and connection. and it’s more powerful than LinkedIn’s algorithm because people respond to stories, not just strategy. Your content can rank well and still fall flat, because what actually gets someone to comment, message, or buy? **Emotion**. That’s the Human Algorithm.

We recently talked about this on our [YOUmanize™ Your Brand Podcast.](https://youtu.be/Vp7QrCHOz6Y?si=hvOAloHD5GiNeqtJ) It’s the unseen engine that powers every meaningful click, DM, and conversation. People don’t engage with automation (obviously). They engage with actual humans, with stories, with opinions, with real moments that remind them they’re not alone.

And if you’re scratching your chin, still unsure what to share, here’s a few suggestions to get you started:** **

🔵 [A behind-the-scenes fail](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuablee_leadership-entrepreneur-mindset-activity-7341834722479640576-sDp4?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAApciIMByUxTZ0oDjJenExsOWihjaHVGITQ)

🔵 [A vulnerable win](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuablee_linkedingrowth-contentstrategy-activity-7346183420051365902-Cp3L?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAApciIMByUxTZ0oDjJenExsOWihjaHVGITQ)

🔵 [A messy lesson](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuablee_sora2-ai-creatoreconomy-activity-7384958906235752448-w-Nj?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAApciIMByUxTZ0oDjJenExsOWihjaHVGITQ)

If you want to see synergy on LinkedIn don’t try to “hack the feed.” Become the person people remember, not just the expert they scroll past. You literally can’t out algorithm someone who’s out connecting you 😂

### How Has LinkedIn’s Shift to Search First Content Changed the Game?

LinkedIn’s shift to search first means every post, comment, and carousel is indexed like a mini blog, making tone, clarity, and human relevance important to showing up in search and staying visible.

So why are most people still posting like it’s 2020? Firing off feed filler posts or cranking out keyword stuffed newsletters, then hoping LinkedIn’s algorithm will do the heavy lifting. But what’s actually happening is this… your content is now part of a living, searchable portfolio, and if you’re not writing like a real person, you might as well be invisible.

Want some quick wins to show up in the right searches?

🔵 Sound like a person (like YOU)

🔵 Write like you're helping one specific person and not broadcasting to thousands

🔵 Share stories, and real life learnings based on your actual life and work experience

This is why LinkedIn content written in a conversational tone gets more visibility and engagement than overly polished, formal posts. It’s allllll about showing up AND being found. That’s what this[LinkedIn News article](https://www.linkedin.com/news/story/human-made-ad-trend-challenges-ai-7292017/) confirms: brands like Cadbury and Apple are betting on human made content because it connects, and that connection… it converts.

### Why Is Human Centered Content Still Your Most Valuable Asset?

Because in a digital world overloaded with automation, what actually builds trust, loyalty, and buying decisions is _human relatability_. AI can mimic tone and structure, but it can’t replicate your lived experience, your values, or the emotional nuance that makes people _feel something_.

Human centered content is what makes your brand memorable, not just visible. It's your edge in a world where everyone has access to the same tools, but not the same story, not the same truth, and not the same ability to connect. That’s why your voice, your vulnerability, and your vision are still your most powerful marketing assets heading into 2026.

what-sets-successful-entrepreneurs-apart.body:
What should entrepreneurs focus on during National Entrepreneurship Month? Gratitude, and not the fluffy kind, I'm talking about a clear, strategic lens that helps real founders avoid burnout, reclaim energy, and build businesses that actually fuel them.

## Entrepreneurship Isn’t Just Hustle, It’s Identity

November is National Entrepreneurship Month, a time to honor the [33.2 million entrepreneurs](https://www.demandsage.com/entrepreneurship-statistics/)in the U.S. who’ve chosen a different path. The ones who didn’t wait for permission, who saw opportunity in the chaos, and who decided to build something of their own.

Entrepreneurship isn’t all Zen and innovation, its long nights, failed launches, doubting your own voice, and wondering if this was a crazy idea. As someone who’s built (and rebuilt) multiple businesses, I’ve come to realize that success doesn’t just come from action. It comes from alignment, and gratitude is one of the most underused, but most powerful tools in a founder’s toolbox.

Gratitude helps you regulate your energy, see failure as fuel, and return to service over ego. It brings you back to your "why", which is often the first thing to fade when you're buried in notifications and KPIs. In honor of National Entrepreneurship Month, I want to share what I call:

## The Gratitude Stack: A 3 Part Entrepreneurial Reset

You don’t need another productivity hack; you need a moment to reset and realign with what really matters.

### 1. How Can Gratitude Help You Manage Your Energy as an Entrepreneur?

Running a business doesn’t just cost money, it costs energy, and most founders are overspending. Gratitude is how you track the ROI of your energy, not just where your time goes… but where your fire goes. When you’re grateful, you’re more attuned to what’s working (and what’s wearing you down).

Try this 3-minute daily check-in:

🔵 What gave me energy today?

🔵 What drained me?

🔵 What can I appreciate in that awareness?

Over time, you’ll start to see patterns. That client who lights you up vs. the one who doesn't. The work that excites you vs. the stuff you procrastinate. And you can begin designing your business around what fuels you, not just what pays the bills. This is how you shift from grind mode to growth mode.

### 2. Why Should Entrepreneurs Be Grateful for Failure?

Because failure is feedback, and gratitude turns it into momentum. Entrepreneurs don’t fail because they’re weak, they fail because they take risks others won’t. But when failure happens, our instinct is to retreat, to hide it, bury it, or pretend it didn’t happen.

Gratitude asks you to sit with it and ask better questions:

🟠 What lesson did this failure teach me?

🟠 What clarity did I gain about my values or direction?

🟠 What doors opened because of it?

When I lost $1.3 million in one business venture, it nearly broke me. But that pain clarified my next move, it revealed what I wouldn’t compromise on again. And it made me a better leader, partner, and father. [According to 2025 U.S. data,](https://www.demandsage.com/entrepreneurship-statistics/)only 10% of startups succeed long-term. But 90% of entrepreneurs are self-made, that means they keep showing up, learning, and adjusting. Gratitude is what helps them keep going.

### 3. How Does Gratitude Anchor Entrepreneurs in Service (Not Just Sales)?

When you’re only focused on revenue, every ‘NO’ feels personal. But when you’re anchored in service, every 'YES' feels earned. Gratitude reminds you that entrepreneurship is bigger than you. It’s about the value you bring, the people you impact, and the difference your business makes, even if no one sees it today.

Ask yourself:

🔵 Who did I serve this week?

🔵 Where did I make someone feel seen, heard, or empowered?

🔵 Who do I need to thank for helping me lead better?

It’s easy to lose sight of the human part of business, but that’s the part that lasts. The part that builds brand trust, client loyalty, and team culture. Metrics matter but meaning matters more.

### Ready to Rewire Your Entrepreneurial Mindset?

The most successful entrepreneurs don’t just hustle harder, they reflect deeper, they reconnect to their mission, they learn from their failures, and they lead with gratitude.

This National Entrepreneurship Month, build your Gratitude Stack:

✅ Audit your energy

✅ Learn from what didn’t work

✅ Focus on service, not ego

And remember: your business doesn’t grow unless _you_ grow. So be the entrepreneur who leads with clarity, not chaos. Happy National Entrepreneurship Month, my friends.

what-should-every-leader-ask-before-q4-e.title: What Should Every Leader Ask Before Q4 Ends? The 3 Conversations That Will Define Your 2026
what-should-every-leader-ask-before-q4-e.excerpt: Why do most leaders blow Q1 of the next year? Because they coast through Q4, avoid the hard conversations, and assume clarity will magically show up on January 1st. We’ve all been there,…
what-should-every-leader-ask-before-q4-e.body:
Why do most leaders blow Q1 of the _next_ year? Because they coast through Q4, avoid the hard conversations, and assume clarity will magically show up on January 1st. We’ve all been there, October hits and suddenly everything is _go-mode_.

Deadlines. Contracts. Planning meetings. A dozen Slack/Teams threads. Q4 is often mistaken for a finish line, but in reality? It’s where Q1 begins. The problem is, most leaders don’t realize they’ve lost Q1 until they wake up in January feeling behind, disconnected, and unsure why their team or clients are suddenly “quiet.” You don’t lose momentum in Q1, you lose it by skipping the hard conversations in Q4.

The foundation for next year’s growth isn’t built in January, it’s built right now, before the ball drops, before the inbox explodes, before you convince yourself “you’ll figure it out after the holidays.” So let’s talk about the 3 conversations every founder, CEO, and leader should have _before_ the year ends.

### 1. The Team Conversation - “What didn’t I hear this year?”

"What didn’t I hear this year?" This is not your standard “year in review.”  It’s not about metrics, KPIs, or surface level success. It’s about what your team _didn’t_ say. What they held back. What you missed in the noise of building, selling, delivering, and leading. According to[Harvard Business Review](https://hbr.org/2025/05/are-you-really-a-good-listener), when employees feel heard by leadership, engagement skyrockets and trust deepens. But when they _don’t_ feel heard? That’s when disconnection grows.

And here’s the trap leaders fall into: we think “quiet” means everything’s okay. But sometimes silence is just filtered truth, and filtered truth is the fastest path to disengagement.

People don’t always speak up when:
- They don’t feel psychologically safe
- They fear conflict or being misunderstood
- They’re too burned out to initiate the hard talk
- They assume nothing will change

Ask your team:
- “What did you want to say but didn’t?”
- “Where did I miss the mark?”
- “What are you carrying that I haven’t noticed?”

You don’t need answers today, you need space to hear what’s real. That’s what leadership looks like, holding space, not just setting direction. At [StandOut Authority](https://www.linkedin.com/company/standoutauthority/) our end-of-year rituals aren’t just performance reviews, they’re real conversations about how people are feeling, what needs to shift, and where we missed the signal. That reflection is what gives us momentum _and_ connection in Q1.

### 2. The Client Conversation - “What changed for you this year?”

Clients don’t walk away  just because you messed up, they walk away because they feel misunderstood, or worse, irrelevant to your process. This time of year is when many clients reevaluate everything. Their budgets. Their goals. Their providers. And if you’re assuming everything’s good just because they renewed last quarter… you might be missing their quiet shift out the door.

Companies restructure. Teams rotate. Priorities evolve. And what once felt aligned might now feel outdated. Take a page from the [Nokia playbook](https://www.thomasnet.com/insights/9-companies-that-failed-to-adapt-to-disruption-and-paid-the-ultimate-price/)… or rather, what _not_ to do. Back in 2007, Nokia held over 50% of global mobile profits. By 2013? That number had dropped to 3%. Why? They failed to adapt. They stopped asking the right questions. They assumed what _was_ working would _keep_ working.

Don’t be Nokia. Ask your clients:
- “What shifted for you this year?”
- “What are you navigating that I might not see?”
- “What would make this partnership more valuable in 2026?”

These questions open the door to trust, retention, and growth. They also protect your Q1 revenue _before_ it’s on the line.

### 3. The Self Conversation: “What did I avoid… and why?”

Let’s get real: the hardest conversation is usually the one you avoid with yourself. This isn’t about judgment, it’s about honesty.

🟠 What decisions did you delay in 2025?

🟠 What conversations did you put off?

🟠 Where did fear, perfectionism, or burnout lead you to say “later” … and never come back?

Peter Drucker, the Austrian-American writer, consultant, and social philosopher widely known as the _inventor of modern management_, once said: “Follow effective action with quiet reflection. From the quiet reflection will come even more effective action.”

That’s what this conversation is about. Not beating yourself up but slowing down long enough to stop operating from survival mode. Because when you’re leading a business, a family, or a team, what you avoid doesn’t just disappear. It compounds.

Start here:
- “What have I been avoiding because I’m afraid of the outcome?”
- “Where am I using busyness to avoid facing the truth?”
- “What would I let go of if I was being radically honest?”

Stillness reveals what busyness buries. And you can’t lead with clarity in Q1 if you’re still hiding from the truth in Q4. For me, some of my clearest leadership moments this year came when I slowed down long enough to ask myself: “What am I pretending not to see?” That question alone reshaped how I parent, how I lead, and how I show up. And I want the same clarity for you.

### You’ve Got 9 Weeks Left in 2025

This is your _real_ new year’s planning window. Not December 31st. Not some offsite in late January. It’s _now._Block the time. Have the conversation. And step into Q1 with clarity, trust, and momentum, not scrambled last minute energy.

So let me ask you again: Which conversation are you most overdue for?

🔵 With your team, to rebuild trust and unlock truth?

🔵 With your clients, to reconnect and realign?

🔵 With yourself, to face what you’ve been avoiding?

Let’s finish this year strong and lead into 2026 with conviction.

how-lead-without-losing-yourself-mental-.excerpt: World Mental Health Day, Why Founders Can’t Sit This One Out October 10th marks World Mental Health Day(https://www.who.int/campaigns/world-mental-health-day/2025), and this year’s theme fr
how-lead-without-losing-yourself-mental-.body:
## World Mental Health Day, Why Founders Can’t Sit This One Out

October 10th marks [World Mental Health Day](https://www.who.int/campaigns/world-mental-health-day/2025), and this year’s theme from the World Federation for Mental Health hits hard: “Mental Health in Catastrophes and Emergencies.” We’re not just talking about war zones or natural disasters. We’re talking about emotional overwhelm, economic pressure, relentless bad news, algorithm anxiety, and the silent collapse happening behind polished Zoom calls. Founders feel it too, because most of the time, we carry the pressure quietly, we lead through chaos while ignoring our own crisis. Entrepreneurs are in their own kind of emergency. And it’s not always visible.

Stats back it up, according to a 2025 survey by [Startup Snapshot,](https://www.startupsnapshot.com/research/the-untold-toll-the-impact-of-stress-on-the-well-being-of-startup-founders-and-ceos/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- 81% of founders don’t speak openly about their mental struggles
- 49% lean only on cofounders or spouses, not trained support
- And nearly everyone reports feeling emotionally isolated during crisis

This year’s campaign isn’t just about awareness. It’s about making mental health accessible, actionable, and real for leaders, especially when the world is in flux. If you're building a business, leading a team, or navigating uncertainty, you’re not just responsible for profits. You’re responsible for the human behind the hustle.

You can’t build a business that thrives if the human behind it is barely surviving. Being a business owner, founder, and now a podcast host, it doesn’t come with a warning label, no one tells you the toll the pressure takes. You just _feel it._ Quietly. Over the past few weeks, as Rachel and I have leaned harder into vulnerability, publicly and privately, we’ve had an overwhelming response. Not in vanity metrics, though those numbers tell a story too. But in DMs. In messages: “Thank you for naming what I’ve felt.”

> **Silence isn’t strength. Vulnerability is.**

### The Hidden Load of Mental Health and the Entrepreneurial Mind

Being an entrepreneur isn’t just about freedom. It means carrying the mental load of…
- Meeting payroll while juggling personal responsibilities.
- Making the hard calls when you don’t want to let anyone down.
- Holding space for your team while hiding your own stress.
- Leading when you’re quietly crumbling.

I’ve shared this before in my book _Balance is Bullsh_t*: you don’t have “work” and “life”. You have _one life_. Trying to keep them separate is what exhausts us. When I went through my divorce, lost millions, and rebuilt everything from scratch… including who I was as a man, a father, a leader, [I realized that burnout wasn’t a badge of honor,](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/why-mental-health-missing-link-modern-leadership-joshua-b-lee-ayazf/)it was a wake-up call and I wish I saw the warning signs sooner.

Now, as I co-run [StandOut Authority](https://www.linkedin.com/company/standoutauthority/) with my wife [Rachel B. Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/therachelblee?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAATthuAB-Gy4FMm8KnvDftaFczqyPAUOIsI) , raise a blended family, and stay real with our community, I choose integration. I’ve let go of the idea of perfection a looooong time ago. Mental health doesn’t just _affect_ your business. It _is_ your business. I’ve seen from my [own experience](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/from-burnout-breakthrough-navigating-stress-leader-joshua-b-lee-j0vlc)when the leader breaks, so does the mission. And surprisingly only a small number of founders seek [external support](https://www.startupsnapshot.com/research/the-untold-toll-the-impact-of-stress-on-the-well-being-of-startup-founders-and-ceos/?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

The leadership shift we need is vulnerability, I believe real leadership shows we bleed, breathe, and struggle, just like everyone else. Launching [YOUmanize Your Brand](https://www.linkedin.com/company/youmanizeyourbrand/) has reminded me: the more I _YOUmanize™_ how I live and lead, the more magnetic my presence becomes. Because people connect with people, not personas, especially in an AI-era drowning in noise.

Shoutout to [Marc Randolph](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_OIIzuHDuG4) (Netflix co‑founder), who speaks with brutal transparency about founder anxiety and resilience. His story reminds us: leadership isn’t spreadsheets. It’s surviving your own doubt.

## Action Over Awareness, What You Can Do Now

Talk is good. But it’s the actions and steps you implement to make a change that truly set great leaders apart from the average. Here’s what I do, and you can also try that helps me stay ‘in my YOUman-zen zone.

🟠 Check in on your team, yes. But also yourself.

🟠 Start the convo privately or publicly but break the silence.

🟠 Set the standard, model boundaries, rest, therapy, and truth.

🟠 Serve, don’t sell, especially this week. Be human first.

## Mental Health Strategies for Entrepreneurs

Awareness is the first step, but you need real strategies to stay in the game without burning out. These are practices I use to protect my mental health:

🔵 **Build Micro‑Routines**You don’t need a 2-hour morning ritual. But you do need anchors in your day. 10 minutes of meditation, a walk after calls, or journaling before bed can reset your nervous system and your perspective.

🔵 **Create a Founder Support Circle**Build a small circle of trusted peers, mentors, or coaches you can speak to without judgment. Sometimes just saying the thing out loud defuses it.

🔵 **Schedule Recovery Like Revenue**If you plan your launches down to the hour, plan your recovery with the same precision. Therapy, workouts, unplugged weekends, they belong on your calendar _before_ you hit the wall.

🔵 **Integrate, Don’t Separate**Stop chasing the myth of “work/life balance.” You don’t have 2 lives, you have one. Blend them with intention: invite family into your wins, share struggles with your team, and let your values run through both.

🔵 **Train Your Team for Transparency**Model it. If you set boundaries, they’ll believe they can too. If you admit when you’re struggling, they’ll bring honesty to you instead of hiding it.

To the founder up at 2AM doubting yourself, to the executive carrying the weight of your team, to the business owner showing up daily but feeling invisible… You are NOT alone. most-powerful-voice-business-one-thats-t.body:
I’ve been thinking about what it really means to use your voice. _Especially_ when it feels risky. Across the country, people are facing real consequences for what they say (_or don’t say_), and the pressure to stay silent is real. Social media has now overtaken TV as the top source of news in the US, [54% of Americans receive news from social media](https://www.theguardian.com/media/2025/jun/17/social-media-overtakes-tv-as-main-source-of-news-in-us-analysis-finds). That means more than half of the population is looking online (and to online voices) for context, clarity, and leadership.

And if you're a founder, a creator, an exec… they’re looking at _YOU._I’m not here to dissect headlines, I’m here to get brutally honest about what it takes to build trust in a high-stakes world. If you take one thing from this edition of my Dopamine Dose, it’s this:

> **You can’t build trust if you’re too afraid to use your voice.**

### Your Voice Doesn’t Have to Be Loud. It Just Has to Be Yours.

In the [first episode](https://youtu.be/-ZgBqF2rZJk?si=0tyupsdp0srL93Uz)of our new podcast _YOUmanize™ Your Brand_, Rachel and I unpack one of the biggest questions we hear from clients and our famiLEE:

**“How do I speak with integrity without putting myself at risk?”**

It’s a real fear. And it’s 100% valid. What I’ve learned (personally and professionally) is this:
- You don’t need to be polarizing to be powerful
- You don’t need to dodge real topics to protect your brand
- You don’t need to be loud to be trusted

A recent [Forbes article](https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbesbusinesscouncil/2025/07/31/how-to-build-customer-trust-in-the-new-digital-world-of-ai-and-why-it-matters/) says companies build trust by consistently doing things _right_. The same applies if YOU are the brand. What you need is ownership of your story, of your values, of the message you repeat and reinforce. If you’re not saying it, someone else will fill the silence for you. For me, that means being crystal clear on my stance, showing up authentically on my LinkedIn and other social platforms AND being open to conversations that might not align with my viewpoint 100%.

## What Actually Makes Your Voice Discoverable (Hint: It’s Not More Content)

These days, people are more skeptical than ever. The moment you show up online, you’re already being lumped into the “just trying to sell me something” bucket. If you want to be known for who you are personally and professionally, that takes more than just posting. It means being CONSISTENT with your messaging and vocal about your values.

If you’re not clear about who you are and what you stand for, the algorithm (and your audience) has no idea how to find you. I’ve been in this online space for a few decades now, and I’ve weathered the social media storms, from Myspace to Facebook to LinkedIn and everything in between, here’s how I’ve made sure my voice doesn’t just get heard, but actually gets recognized by people, by platforms, EVEN by AI. What Builds Trust and Discoverability

🔵 **I stay in my lane.** I don’t post about everything. I talk about LinkedIn, entrepreneurship, AI, brand trust, leadership, and human-first business. When you stick to your pillars, you train people (and platforms) to understand what you’re known for.

🔵 **I repeat myself on purpose.** I’ve been publishing _Dopamine Dose_ for over two years, and I’ve said some version of the same message hundreds of times. It’s personal branding.

🔵 **I post where it counts.** LinkedIn is indexed by both Google and OpenAI. Because I show up there regularly with the same voice and values, I’ve had people discover me just by asking ChatGPT about trusted LinkedIn experts. That happened on purpose and by alignment.

### What Breaks Trust and Gets You Ignored

🔴 **Trend-hopping.** If you change your message every week, people stop paying attention. The algorithm does too.

🔴 **Mixed signals.** Saying one thing on a podcast, another in a post, and another in a sales call? That’s just confusing and will reflect poorly on you.

🔴 **Performing instead of positioning.** If you’re just chasing attention with hot takes or viral bait, you might get clicks but not credibility.

I’ve learned that you don’t need to yell to be heard. You need to show up, say what matters, and keep saying it until both your audience _and_ the algorithm know it’s you. That’s how you build a voice that gets remembered.

### Why Loud Doesn’t Mean Aligned

I’m not here to tell you what to say or how to say it. But after 20+ years in this game, I’ve tried it all. If you’ve followed me, you know, I chased the clicks, I counted the cash… and I nearly lost myself in the process. The real flex? Showing up with your _whole_ voice, not just your highlight reel.

And honestly, the last few weeks have been a hard reminder of how risky that can feel. From Colbert and Kimmel to Texas teachers and university presidents, people are being _punished_, not for saying something reckless, but for standing in their truth. I don’t agree with what’s happened to them. Silencing people for showing up honestly isn’t leadership, it’s fear in a costume. Because when you mute your voice to fit in, you lose the very thing people trust you for.

Sooooo… can we stop treating our brands like content factories? Anddddd…. can we start focusing on courageous connection instead? That’s what [Rachel B. Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/therachelblee?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAATthuAB-Gy4FMm8KnvDftaFczqyPAUOIsI) and I are building with [YOUmanize Your Brand](https://www.linkedin.com/company/youmanizeyourbrand/) . And that’s what I want for you, too. Your voice doesn’t need to be loud. It doesn’t need to be perfect. It just needs to be true.

In a world suffocating with noise, clarity becomes your breath of fresh air and authority. So if you’re waiting for permission to speak… this IS it. why-great-leaders-outlast-ai-lazy-ones-w.body:
## AI Can’t Lead People. That’s Your Job.

Someone who understands how to use AI can replace you. But AI itself? It can’t. In the AI era, effective leadership is still one thing: _human_. Let’s get clear on what that really means.

We’re not just living through a technological upgrade. We’re living through a leadership reckoning. For the first time in history, disruption isn’t just coming for the factory floor. It’s coming for the boardroom. The strategist. The brand builder. The middle manager. It’s not just physical labor that’s being automated, it’s thinking.

> This is the part no one wants to talk about. The quiet reality being whispered in boardrooms is this: Your role may not be safe just because you’re smart. If a machine can replicate your value faster and cheaper, you’re already on borrowed time.

But here’s the thing: AI still can’t lead. It can execute. It can optimize. It can simulate. But it can’t feel, guide, or connect. It can’t coach someone through self-doubt, rally a team behind a shared vision, or create a movement.  It doesn’t know what matters, it just knows what’s next.

That’s _your_ job.

In this moment, leadership isn’t about being the expert.  It’s about being the one who’s brave enough to lead through uncertainty. To name what’s changing. To invite others into the evolution. And to do it all without a playbook. You don’t need to have it all figured out. But you _do_ need to be the one willing to face it head-on, because waiting it out isn’t leadership.

The question isn’t whether AI will change everything.  It’s whether you’re ready to lead through that change.

## Machines Need Managers, Not More Code

You can’t delegate your AI strategy and expect to stay relevant. The biggest mistake I see leaders making right now? They treat AI like an IT project, not a business transformation. They toss it to the ops team, wait for a dashboard to get built, and pat themselves on the back for being “forward-thinking.” Meanwhile, the 1% of CEOs who actually get it? They’re building AI into the bones of their business.

They’re not just using the tools. They’re rebuilding workflows, retraining teams, rethinking value, and they’re doing it from the top down. If you’re a founder, exec, or leader reading this and you're not personally involved in how AI is being adopted in your company, you’re not leading the future. You’re reacting to it. And you better believe someone hungrier, scrappier, or smarter is already outpacing you.

AI isn’t here to make your team 10% faster, it’s here to change what your team even is. We’re shifting from role-based orgs to skill-based orgs. From headcount planning to AI augmented productivity, from task execution to decision acceleration.

[Shopify’s CEO](https://www.forbes.com/sites/douglaslaney/2025/04/09/selling-ai-strategy-to-employees-shopify-ceos-manifesto/) just made AI adoption part of employee performance reviews. Think about that. Before teams can ask for more people, they have to prove AI _can’t_ do the job first. That’s not a cost-cutting play, that’s a culture shift, that’s leadership that isn’t waiting around to get disrupted, it’s building a team that’s disruption-proof.

> The question isn’t, “How can we use AI to save money?” It’s: “How do we reimagine what’s possible when machines do what they’re best at and our people get to do the rest?”

## Leadership in the AI Era Isn’t Optional

If AI is impacting every role, every team, and every customer interaction, then as a leader, this is your job now. Not later. Now. This transformation? It will not wait for your next quarterly offsite. You don’t need to become an engineer. But you do need to ask the hard questions:

🔵 What does value creation look like when 50% of tasks can be automated?

🔵 What does leadership look like when your people are managing AI, not each other?

🔵 How does your brand evolve when content, strategy, and ops can all be accelerated by machines?

Most execs are still sitting back, hoping someone on their team figures it out. That’s not leadership. That’s hiding.

### 3 Things Real Leaders Are Doing Right Now

- **Act Before You're Told**Leadership doesn’t wait for permission. The leaders who win in this next era aren’t asking, _“Should we try AI?”_ They’re already building it into their strategy, their decision making, their creative process. If you’re still in “wait and see” mode, you’re already behind.
- **Make Your Expertise Visible**In this era, _quiet expertise gets passed over_. The people getting hired, funded, promoted, and invited into the room? They’re the ones sharing their POV, showing their thinking, owning their story. If you’re not visible, someone less qualified is winning the game, because perception is reality.
- **Build a Brand That Doesn’t Blend In**AI made the internet louder, way louder. The only way to stand out now? Clarity. That means a message that hits, a voice that’s yours, a presence people feel. If you’re not intentionally building that, you're in a race against machines that don’t get tired and don’t care if they sound generic.How every CEO feels right about now.

stop-spamming-3-ways-build-trusted-brand.body:
### Spam Will Never Build Real Influence

There’s a big difference between attention and trust. Last week, I found out someone used my name, without permission, to try and sell their program to every single attendee on our event list. They didn’t connect. They didn’t engage. They didn’t build community.

They scraped names and sent mass, automated messages… pretending we were affiliated. This wasn’t just a bad marketing move; it was a betrayal of trust. They hijacked a space that Rachel and I intentionally built for human connection. If you're building your brand around spammy tactics and stolen audiences, you're not just burning bridges, you’re torching your reputation.

Most people don’t realize the cost of that kind of behavior. It’s not just about losing a sale. When you approach people this way, you lose their trust. You lose their respect. And you lose their openness to ever hearing from you again.

That kind of damage spreads quickly. In today’s world, where word-of-mouth travels at the speed of screenshots, one unethical move doesn’t stay private for long. The ripple effect can be significant, not only for your credibility but for how people perceive your brand moving forward.

People remember how you make them feel. And when your outreach feels manipulative or transactional, that feeling sticks. No clever copy or slick funnel will undo it. So when someone uses automation to bypass relationship building, it's not just a poor tactic, it’s a reflection of their values. It shows they’re not here to serve, they’re here to extract.

And what concerns me most is that this isn’t an isolated incident. It’s a symptom of a larger problem in how people are taught to do business online. We’ve entered a digital culture that encourages speed over sincerity, automation over authenticity, and visibility over values. None of those shortcuts lead to meaningful, sustainable growth.

The brands that thrive now and will continue to thrive, are the ones rooted in trust, transparency, and connection. They’re led by people who understand that influence isn’t earned through manipulation. It’s earned through consistency, care, and a genuine commitment to showing up as a human first.

That’s why what happened last week matters. Not just for me and Rachel. Not just for our event. But for every business owner, entrepreneur, and brand builder who’s trying to do this the right way. Because if we don’t speak up and call this out for what it is, the line between connection and exploitation gets even blurrier. And for me, that line isn’t negotiable.

🔵 We’re here to build communities, not contact lists.

🔵 We’re here to foster trust, not transactions.

🔵 We’re here to YOUmanize™ the brand, not systematize the soul out of it.

Spam might get you a few clicks. But it will never earn you trust. And trust is the only thing that scales.

### Reputation Is Still Your Most Valuable Currency

You might get a reply. You might even close a deal. But the long-term cost? It’s bigger than most people realize. We’re living in an era where[trust is the new ROI.](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/what-smart-founders-know-listening-linkedin-success-joshua-b-lee-rzgjc) And on the flip side? The moment someone feels tricked or used, your brand equity goes down the drain.

Your digital footprint is forever, and your outreach strategy is your reputation. Everything you post, comment, share, or message online leaves a trail. And while your inbox might feel private, screenshots move fast. Trust me, our team saw this firsthand. That’s why the small moments matter.

✅ A thoughtful comment that helps someone feel seen.

✅ A message that genuinely adds value.

✅ A piece of content that sparks curiosity without selling.

This is the type of influence that lasts. Our clients have landed 6-figure deals, not from content calendars or fancy funnels, but from one meaningful DM, one authentic connection, one well timed post that hit the right person at the right time. This isn’t theory, it’s what we live and breathe every single day.

Take the client testimonial below, it’s proof of synergy. When someone publicly acknowledges how you impacted them, that impression doesn’t just reflect back on you in the moment, it filters down into everything you do. It influences how others perceive your brand, how opportunities flow your way, and how much long-term trust you build.

### 3 Small Shifts to Build Real Influence

Want to stop sounding like a bot and start sounding like _you_? Here’s where to begin:

✅ **Ditch the templates.** Rewrite your messages as if you were texting a friend, with care, not copy-paste.

✅ **Comment to connect.** Ask a real question. Don’t just drop emojis or “Great post!” replies.

✅ **Post with purpose.** Share insights your audience can use _today_, not a thought bubble from your journal.

These small actions build trust that stacks, reputations that compound, and brands that grow without manipulation. When I founded [StandOut Authority](https://www.linkedin.com/company/standoutauthority/), I wasn’t just reacting to the noise. I was responding to a deeper need: The need for real, [human-first connection](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/why-showing-up-clearly-beats-selling-todays-digital-world-lee-tsfyc)in the professional space. We’re not anti-tech. We’re anti-fake. Because automation without intention is just noise.

So we built something different:

🟠 Messaging that sounds like _you_, not your CRM

🟠 Content that sparks conversations, not just click

🟠 Community that grows organically, without cold DMs

🟠 Thought leadership that builds trust, without selling your soul

This is the YOUmanize™ Your Brand methodology. And it’s the heart of everything we teach and live out daily, with our clients and our team.

### Let’s Keep This Conversation Going

Have you ever had someone hijack your list? Or send a message using your name without permission? How did you handle it? What did it teach you? Drop a comment or send me a DM, I want to hear your experience. This needs to be a community conversation, not a solo soapbox. Because this isn’t just about us. It’s about all of us who are building something real online.

how-open-minded-business-leaders-can-use.body:
In the age of algorithms, your intuition is the one advantage the internet can’t replicate. Last fall, I sat in a packed conference room, listening to a “copy this to go viral” keynote. The speaker had energy. The slides were sharp. The catchy TikTok hooks were polished. But something didn’t land.

It wasn’t that the tactics were wrong, it’s that they weren’t _mine_. There was no connection to purpose, no deeper _why_. It felt like chasing metrics for the sake of metrics. The next morning, I brought this to my team: What’s real? What’s fake? And how do we make sure the people we serve can tell the difference the second they engage with us?

I’ve managed nearly a billion in ad spend and overseen 35 trillion online impressions, and here’s what I know: the only metric that compounds over time is human connection. Humanetics calls it “human-centric design”, creating experiences that are functional, inclusive, and deeply resonant. In business, you are the product. And if you want to stand out, you have to show up with radical authenticity, not a recycled formula.

Copying someone else’s playbook is easy. But easy doesn’t lead. Your voice, your _real_ voice, lives at the intersection of your soul and your intuition. That’s where trust begins, and that’s where your best strategy is born.

## What Human Design Is (and Why It Matters in Leadership and Business)

If you haven’t heard of it, [Human Design](https://ahumandesign.com/the-science-behind-human-design-an-exploration-of-the-physics-and-genetics-underlying-the-system/) is a decision-making and self-awareness framework that combines ancient wisdom and modern science, drawing from astrology, the I Ching, Kabbalah, and quantum physics, to give you a “user manual” for how you operate at your best.

It identifies:
- **Your Type**: how your energy works best.
- **Your Authority**: how you’re built to make decisions.

There’s no “good” or “bad” type, just the most aligned way for _you_ to work, lead, and create. For me, I’m a _Generator with Emotional Authority._ That means my best results happen when I respond to opportunities that truly light me up and I wait for emotional clarity before making a big decision.

## The Invisible Gap in Modern Leadership

Back when I was deep in the billion-dollar ad ecosystem, I thought I had the formula: more reach, more impressions, more numbers on the board. But even with those wins, something still felt… off. It wasn’t burnout. It wasn’t lack of opportunity. It was the quiet realization that I was building by someone else’s rules.

Most leaders I meet today are still stuck in one of two playbooks:

## What Leadership Alignment Looks Like in Real Life

Knowing my Human Design changed everything about how I lead and create. It’s why I say NO to opportunities that look good on paper but trigger doubt inside me. It’s why I don’t force a rigid schedule, but instead work in bursts of inspired momentum.

When I honor this emotional rhythm:

## 3 Ways to Test Your Leadership Alignment This Week

If you want to see how aligned you really are, try this:

- **Observe**: Catch yourself ignoring that gut feeling. What happens next? More clarity, or more frustration?
- **Experiment**: Make one decision this week purely on what feels right, not what you think you’re supposed to do.

When you stop forcing it, the right opportunities start responding. The leaders we remember, the ones who move markets, inspire loyalty, and create real change, don’t start with _what_ to do. They start with _why_ they do it. That’s what alignment is. It’s knowing yourself so well that every move you make is an extension of your purpose. It’s the confidence to ignore the noise, to resist the pressure to be everything to everyone, and to instead show up where you can make the greatest impact.

When you lead from that place, your strategy becomes more than a plan,  it becomes a reflection of who you are. And that’s the one thing no competitor, no algorithm, and no AI can ever duplicate. The question is: are you leading from the inside out, or letting the outside in? ### Why Most Experts Stay Invisible on LinkedIn (Even When They’re Brilliant)

When I stopped chasing volume and started aligning with what truly builds authority, trust signals, human connection, and strategic positioning, everything shifted. LinkedIn is quietly evaluating whether you are credible. It is measuring your recommendations, your visual presence, the coherence of your messaging. This is why a profile that looks polished but says nothing real about you does not convert, it lacks the proof decision-makers are looking for.

**3. The Relationship Graph**

This is where your network either elevates you or holds you back. If the people around you are not engaging with you in meaningful ways, LinkedIn assumes you are not relevant, and you stop showing up in the places where decisions happen.

This is why posting more is not the answer. You cannot out hustle an algorithm that is scanning for depth. You have to build the signals it trusts. And once you do, you stop chasing and start attracting.

Imagine opportunities finding you instead of you constantly pushing for them. Imagine decision-makers coming into your inbox already convinced you are the person they need to work with.

ai-wont-replace-great-leaders-average-on.body:
## AI Won’t Replace You. But Someone Who Knows How to Use It Might.

Let’s not sugarcoat this. AI isn’t hype anymore, it’s here, and it’s already reshaping industries faster than any of us expected. [Goldman Sachs](https://www.gspublishing.com/content/research/en/reports/2023/03/27/d64e052b-0f6e-45d7-967b-d7be35fabd16.html) predicts 300 million jobs will be disrupted globally in the next decade. [Geoffrey Hinton](https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/geoffrey-hinton-these-jobs-will-be-replaced-due-to-ai/493388), the so-called “Godfather of AI,” [said it bluntly](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=giT0ytynSqg&ab_channel=TheDiaryOfACEO): _“It’ll replace everybody.”_

Does that mean it’s game over for leaders, founders, and entrepreneurs? Not even close. The truth is this: AI isn’t coming for your job. But someone who knows how to use it absolutely is. In every major shift, electricity, the internet, mobile, there are two types of people:
- Those who panic, resist, and get left behind.
- And those who adapt, lead, and build the next wave of opportunity.

So which one are you going to be?

### You’re Not Competing with People Anymore

You’re competing with bots. Here’s the harsh reality: if your role can be boiled down to a set of instructions, AI will eventually learn how to do it, faster, cheaper, and without coffee breaks. But here’s the opportunity: AI is still just a tool. It needs humans, real leaders, who know how to prompt it, train it, and guide it. And there’s one thing no algorithm or robot will ever have: _a personal brand._

In this new world, your personal brand is essential and it's your protection plan. It’s how you cut through the noise, attract the right opportunities, and prove your value beyond what any machine can do.

### Your Personal Brand Is Your Protection Plan

The next generation entering the workforce won’t just be competing with other graduates, they’ll be competing with bots. Degrees are starting to look the same. Job titles are as fluid as water. And résumés? Half of them sound like they were written by ChatGPT. I think about this every day because I’ve got two teenagers at home. In the next 5–7 years, they’ll step into a job market unlike anything we’ve seen before. And here’s the advice I give them:

> **Your voice is the one thing that makes you irreplaceable.**

In a world where machines can process data faster and churn out content at scale, people don’t want to follow robots. They want to follow humans, **leaders with a point of view**, a story, and the courage to show up authentically. This is why your personal brand ad a leader isn’t optional anymore. It’s essential. It’s how you cut through the noise, attract opportunities, and prove your value beyond what any machine can replicate.

Let me clear up a few misconceptions:

**🔵 Content isn’t a vanity metric. It’s visibility.** Done right, it shows the world what you stand for and invites people to buy into you before they ever buy from you.

**🔵 Publishing equals positioning.** Every post is a breadcrumb, every comment a handshake, every video a signal. When you share content that aligns with your values and goals, you’re putting yourself in the driver’s seat of your career.

**🔵 People don’t follow perfection. They follow people.** The best leaders don’t wait until they’re “ready.” They show up, share their voice, and refine as they go.

The AI revolution will amplify the leaders who lead with authenticity and greatness and erase the ones who don’t.

### 3 Shifts to Stay Relevant in the AI Era

- **Learn the damn tools.** You don’t have to code or build your own GPTs. But if you can’t prompt, delegate, or optimize with AI… someone else in your space will. And they’ll outpace you, not because they’re smarter, but because they evolved with the times.
- **Use AI to scale your thinking, not replace it.** AI is great for brainstorming, organizing, and repurposing. But the big ideas? The original insights? That’s on you. That’s your edge.
- **Lead like a human.** AI still needs a human on the other end to make decisions, translate nuance, and connect emotionally. Emotional intelligence will be the ultimate competitive advantage in an AI-driven world.Meme Image Source imgflip

### Great Leaders Adapt. Average Ones Get Replaced.

I know what it’s like to get caught chasing the wrong metrics. Years ago, I was running massive ad campaigns, pulling in billions of impressions and millions in revenue. On paper, it looked like success. But behind the scenes, I was burning out. I was scaling systems, not connection. Moving fast but going nowhere meaningful. That’s the same trap I see leaders falling into with AI today.

It’s easy to get seduced by automation and shortcuts. To think more technology equals better leadership. But the leaders who win in this next chapter won’t be the ones automating the fastest, they’ll be the ones who know how to cut through the noise, inspire trust, and use AI as a tool, not a crutch. I had to rebuild my approach to leadership from the ground up. And it taught me one simple truth:

> **Sustainable businesses are built by sustainable leaders.**

AI isn’t going to change that. If anything, it’s going to amplify it. The question is: will you rise above average? Or let the machines and the people who know how to lead them, pass you by?

### Lead the Future. Don’t Chase It.

This is the moment for leaders to step up. AI can automate tasks. It can even scale businesses. But it can’t build trust, vision, or a voice people want to follow. That’s your job. And in this next chapter, leaders who do it well will rise above the noise while the rest get replaced.

At [StandOut Authority](https://www.linkedin.com/company/standoutauthority/), we built [Launchpad](https://standoutauthority.com/brandlaunchpad) for this exact moment. It’s for founders, executives, and creators ready to cut through the noise, amplify their authority, and lead in a way AI never can. If you’re ready to stop blending in and start leading at scale, let’s talk.The LinkedIn Brand Launchpad transforms your story and expertise into a presence that attracts opportunities and builds undeniable authority.

I’ve sat in rooms with billionaires. I was there for the LinkedIn launch campaigns that reached millions. And still, I see too many founders and entrepreneurs getting passed over online, not because they aren’t talented, but because their digital presence doesn’t match their real-world impact.

Here’s what happens over and over:
- You’ve built a real business. Delivered real results.
- But online? You’re invisible.
- Meanwhile, people with half your expertise are landing 6-figure deals, stages, and podcasts because they’ve made themselves impossible to ignore.

That’s why Rachel and I created [Launchpad](https://standoutauthority.com/brandlaunchpad), to help founders and execs close that gap. This isn’t about posting more. It’s not about chasing likes. And it’s definitely not about turning into another “LinkedIn guru.” It’s about building a personal brand so strong it does the heavy lifting for you. So when people check you out (and they will), they see the real you:

✅ The authority.

✅ The leader they want in their corner.

If you’re ready to stop blending in and start standing out in the AI era, **we’ve opened 5 spots for leaders** who are serious about owning their voice and their presence. **👉**[Check out Launchpad Here](https://standoutauthority.com/brandlaunchpad)

what-smart-founders-know-listening-linke.body:
### Why the Smartest Founders Don’t Shout, They Listen

Everyone’s trying to be the loudest voice in the feed. More posts. More “hot takes.” More noise. But if everyone’s shouting… who’s actually being heard? Visibility isn’t about volume. It’s about value. The most strategic founders know that cutting through the noise isn’t about yelling louder, it’s about listening sharper.

I’m not talking about being passive. I’m talking about being intentional. Because listening, real, strategic listening, is what turns likes into leads and scrolls into conversations. On LinkedIn, it looks like this:

✔ Reading the room before you post

✔ Responding with purpose, not performance

✔ Paying attention to what your audience is talking about, not just what you want to say

The founders I see winning long-term. They pause before they post. They engage with empathy. And they build real trust by showing up with their audience, not just to them. That’s the Human Algorithm in action. And the best part? This strategy doesn’t just feel better, it performs better. So, the next time you’re tempted to push out another post just to stay visible, try to pause, then listen, and ask yourself: “What conversation do I want to be invited into?”

I was a guest on The Lifestyle Investor Podcast 2 years ago, and what I said then still rings true today. Because the loudest voice might get attention. But the one who actually _gets it_? That’s the voice people trust. How do smart founders turn _listening_ into opportunities on LinkedIn? It’s not about posting more, it’s about paying better attention. Here’s how strategic listening builds authority, deepens relationships, and drives real revenue 👇

### Stop Shouting, Start Noticing

LinkedIn today feels like a holiday rush at the grocery store, everyone’s piling in, rushing to grab attention, hoping their post gets seen. It’s chaotic. And in that chaos, your audience isn’t just scanning for deals… they’re craving to feel seen, understood, and valued. Even the sharpest piece of content will flop if it doesn’t hit that emotional chord. Why? Because connection doesn’t live in the metrics, it lives in the _moments_.At The Council by Archangel, they asked me to speak last minute. I listened first, read the room, then ditched the script I had prepared. I spoke from the heart, sometimes the smartest move is staying quiet long enough to hear what matters.

🔵 What are they _actually_ commenting on?

🔵What are they resharing without being asked?

🔵What questions keep popping up again and again?

That’s where the smart leaders shine, they don’t guess what their audience needs. They _listen_ for it. Sometimes silence is your most powerful move. [Harvard Business Review](https://hbr.org/podcast/2025/06/what-leaders-get-wrong-about-listening)nailed it in a podcast episode called “What Leaders Get Wrong About Listening” (ep. 1029). They found that leaders who truly listen are seen as more competent, more trustworthy, and more human.

Let that sink in. Listening doesn’t make you passive. It makes you powerful. Because influence doesn’t start when you talk, it starts when you _tune in_. Before your audience says a word, the smartest founders are already observing. They’re absorbing the signals. And then? They show up with something that feels so damn relevant, it almost feels like mind-reading.

That’s not luck. That’s leadership. So, the next time you’re stressing about “saying the right thing” … pause. Because in today’s world, the real win isn’t being louder. It’s being more _in tune_.

### The Quiet Move That Builds Loud Results on LinkedIn

Listening on LinkedIn isn’t about lurking in the bushes like a creep. Lurking is passive. It’s scrolling endlessly, consuming content without contributing, observing without engaging. Listening is different. It’s intentional. It’s strategic. It’s powerful.

It means showing up to _understand_. When you listen on LinkedIn with purpose, you’re not doing more than lurking about what’s being said. You’re strategically decoding and analyzing what’s beneath the surface. _You’re identifying patterns, pain points, desires, and doubts that your audience might not even have words for yet._

Here’s what real listening looks like in practice:
- **Read through comment threads** to spot what your audience _isn’t_ saying directly. Look for repeated concerns, confusion, or strong emotional reactions. These are AMAZING clues to unmet needs.
- **Comment back with curiosity**, not conclusions. Ask follow-up questions, open conversational loops, and engage with opinions that differ from yours. Acknowledge what someone shared… Always try to be a mirror, not a microphone.
- **Save thoughtful posts** and reference them in DMs to start deeper conversations. "Saw your take on XYZ and it really stuck with me. I found it helpful when you said XYZ." can open up real dialogue. Lead with value, not sales.
- **Run polls** not to “convert,” but to _understand_. Use the results to validate assumptions, gather content inspiration, or invite follow-up conversations. Polls are a great engagement tool.
- **Create content that reflects what your network actually needs**. You can do this with confidence because they literally told you first. Directly or indirectly, your audience is always signaling what matters. Your job is to capture and reflect it back with clarity and care.

> _If you’re not paying attention to what your audience is already saying, why should they care about what you post?_

When you truly listen, something magical happens. You STOP guessing and start CONNECTING. That’s when your content stops being boring background noise and starts becoming a necessary announcement.

## The 4-Part Framework for Quiet Influence

Reaal connection doesn’t start with a megaphone, it starts with a mindset. Listening on LinkedIn isn’t lurking. It’s a strategy. It’s how you spot the gold _before_ anyone else sees it and turn that into content, conversations, and clients. Here’s how I do it, step by step:

**1. Observe First**Spend 10 minutes a day scanning not your feed, but your ideal client’s comments. Look for patterns. Gaps. Frustrations.

**2. Respond with Curiosity**Ask questions, acknowledge ideas, and avoid one-upping. Show them they’re seen and engage in open-minded conversations. We all have opinions and none of them are wrong.

**3. Reflect and Repurpose**Turn what you’ve learned into “teach me” content. Quote your audience. Let them see themselves in your posts.

**4. DM with Empathy**Send messages that lead with value and connection. Avoid pitching straight away (no one likes that). Try an opening like, “I saw your comment about X and it really stood out…” is one of the most powerful openers you can use.

Success on LinkedIn isn’t luck. It’s backed by data. [LinkedIn & Edelman’s 2024 Thought Leadership Report](https://www.edelman.com/expertise/Business-Marketing/2024-b2b-thought-leadership-report) reveals a clear pattern. Leaders who actively engage beyond their own posts and truly listen to their audience, and then create thought leadership content around this, see far greater results. Guesswork just doesn’t compete.

Ask yourself:

🔵 When did your audience last comment, “This really hit home”?

🔵 Can your ideal client describe what you stand for, without you saying it?

🔵 Have you started conversations lately… without posting?

Your authority won’t come from how much you say. It’ll come from how deeply you understand, listening is no longer a soft skill! To sum it all up… Talk less. Learn more. Lead better.

I dropped some serious truth bombs on the latest episode of[Marketing Minds](https://youtu.be/i0YK8hi5Vww?si=Q8vVQbiLI4RJH-Lo) about my LinkedIn strategy that generated 20 Million views in 3 months. From building human connection in a digital world to navigating entrepreneurship without losing yourself in the algorithm, I brought the realness (and the receipts).

If you’ve ever:

🔵 questioned your relationship with visibility

🔵 struggled with balancing being seen vs. being strategic

🔵 wondered how to scale _without_ selling your soul

…this one’s for you. Thank you, [Aleric Heck](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alericheck?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAAuRB0IBLSp8OeufCE9RHHqhmnpoC_GICmw), for having me on and can’t wait to chat again. Go give it a watch, take notes, and maybe rewatch again. 🎧[Listen to the episode here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=i0YK8hi5Vww)
