why-showing-up-clearly-beats-selling-tod.body:
## Selling Is No Longer the Strategy. Showing Up Is.

Let’s be honest with ourselves, LinkedIn was once a haven for pitch-first behavior. It followed a predictable cycle: connect, pitch, hope for a reply, and repeat. But the world has changed and so has the platform.

People have evolved. They’re more discerning. They crave authenticity, not automation. And LinkedIn? It’s matured into a space where connection matters more than conversion. If you're still showing up like it's 2017, treating every post like a billboard, you’re not just behind the curve. You’ve become invisible.

The data tells a compelling story; [LinkedIn’s 2025 Engagement Report](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/blog/thought-leadership/2025/content-influence-index)confirms that _salesy_ content is a no-no for engagement and growth. Sales-driven content doesn’t just underperform; it actively turns people away. Executives scroll faster. Decision-makers tune out. Why? Because the pitch-first approach lacks something essential: [humanity.](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuablee_socialselling-businessadvice-leadership-activity-7338573236630147073-rJ94?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAApciIMByUxTZ0oDjJenExsOWihjaHVGITQ)We know the quote, we know the man, we need the message.

It’s not that people are against offers. They’re just tired of being sold to by strangers. They want to engage with people who feel real, who stand for something, who show up with purpose. So, if you're not being seen, it’s not because what you offer lacks value. It’s because your presence lacks connection. That’s not a failure, it’s a signal. A call to realign how you’re showing up in the world.

And that’s exactly where our work begins.

## The Visibility Shift

This is no longer about chasing likes or viral one-hit wonders. This is about [sustainable visibility,](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuablee_leadership-entrepreneurship-businessadvice-activity-7336036579435495425-oM35?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAApciIMByUxTZ0oDjJenExsOWihjaHVGITQ) being seen _consistently_ and _clearly_ for who you are, what you believe, and why it matters. Think of visibility as a reputation built in public. Every post, every comment, every shared insight contributes to how others perceive you and more importantly, how they remember you. The question is, are you shaping that perception intentionally, or are you leaving it to chance?

Here's the formula we use:

**Clarity**: Can someone understand what you stand for in 10 seconds or less?

**Consistency**: Are you showing up weekly, or just when inspiration hits?

**Credibility**: Are you sharing _earned_ insights, not regurgitated fluff?

If any one of those is missing, your message doesn’t land. You don’t need to go viral. You need to be memorable. Most leaders are already online. But they’re not truly present. They share updates, but not insight. Headlines, but not heart. And as a result, they’re invisible in plain sight.

If you're a business owner looking to attract new clients and opportunities, the same principle applies. LinkedIn is a trust directory.

## Visibility That Converts: 3 Things We Do Differently (No Selling Required)

We’ve worked with hundreds of leaders across industries. Here’s what we teach:

1️⃣ **The Engagement Engine**

Most people confuse engagement with attention. At Standout Authority, we build engines, not hype. We teach our clients to turn passive eyeballs into two-way conversations by _leading with gratitude,_ sharing real insights, and opening doors through micro-engagement. It’s not about gaming the algorithm. It’s about honoring the human behind the screen.

Someone likes your post? That’s an open door. Someone visits your profile? That’s a spark. Most miss these moments. We turn them into relationships.

2️⃣ **The Human Algorithm**

We teach leaders to show up as _themselves_, the real version that existed before the job title, the TEDx talk, or the 8-figure exit. Why? Because connection is built through [shared experience.](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuablee_linkedin-contentstrategy-leadership-activity-7315742838418284544-m70f?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAApciIMByUxTZ0oDjJenExsOWihjaHVGITQ)If you never show them where you’ve struggled, they’ll never believe you can help them rise. This isn’t about being vulnerable for the sake of it. It’s about being relatable. That’s what builds trust.

3️⃣ **The 70/20/10 Content Rhythm**

Content isn’t king. Quality content is queen.

✔️ 70% is high-value, actionable insight, what we call “building authority” content.

✔️ 20% is social proof, milestones, wins, credibility builders.

✔️ 10% is personal, family, mindset, moments that make you human.

This ratio is how we help leaders dominate feeds _without pitching._

## A Lesson to Learn from the CEO Who Stopped Hiding

Microsoft was once a tech giant with zero personality. Cold. Unapproachable. Enter Satya Nadella. He didn’t just change strategy. He changed _how he showed up._He started posting insights, not press releases. He talked about fatherhood. Empathy. How he sees AI reshaping society. He opened the curtain and let people see _the man behind the CEO badge.__Photo Source: Leverage Edu_

And here’s what happened: Engagement skyrocketed. Trust increased. Culture shifted. Microsoft became _relevant_ again, not because of a product launch, but because of a personal rebrand. His content wasn’t glossy. It was grounded. And that’s what made it powerful.__According to [Talent-E](https://www.talent-e.io/blog/what-ceos-can-learn-from-satya-nadellas-personal-branding-strategy/), Nadella’s personal brand played a huge role in rebuilding Microsoft’s culture and making the company feel relevant again. He didn’t have to be flashy, he just had to be R-E-A-L.

That’s the power of visibility. It doesn’t just boost engagement. It shifts perception. And when a leader makes that shift, it filters through the entire organization.

## The Visibility Test

Here’s the test I challenge every leader and founder to take:

🔵 When’s the last time your ideal client shared your post with their team?

🔵 Would they know how to introduce you if someone asked, “What do they actually do?”

🔵 Have you published something lately that made someone DM you, “That hit different”?

These questions measure more than marketing. They measure meaning. [73% of decision-makers](https://www.edelman.com/insights/thought-leadership-gets-b2b-buyers-back-into-game#:~:text=A%20striking%2073%25%20of%20B2B,working%20with%20a%20current%20supplier.)say they trust thought leadership more than polished marketing or product decks when it comes to judging what a company’s really capable of. That’s not about volume. That’s about voice.

Authority is built by showing up at the right place at the right time and doing it consistently over time. You don’t need to be the smartest voice in the room. You need to be the clearest. Show up with one core belief. Say it in a way only you can. Then repeat it with conviction. Some may say I don't belong in certain rooms, but here I am ... because I've always been my most authentic self.

Stop asking, _“How do I sell more?”_ Start asking, _“How do I make them remember me?”_In a world where content comes and goes, what stays is _who_ you are and _how_ you show up. Take it from a guy who’s been where you are, stressed about not having a solid online presence, despite being a leader in my field. You don’t need more posts. You need more purpose. You don’t need more tactics. You need more truth.

Let’s normalize clear over clever. The right people will tune in to hear your authentic voice. Keep it real and don’t overcomplicate it.  Want to be seen for what you stand for? Show up. Stand out. Serve first.

## ICYMI 🎙️🎧

I dropped some serious truth bombs on the latest episode of [Marketing Minds](https://youtu.be/i0YK8hi5Vww?si=Q8vVQbiLI4RJH-Lo) about my LinkedIn strategy that generated 20 Million views in 3 months. From building human connection in a digital world to navigating entrepreneurship without losing yourself in the algorithm, I brought the realness (and the receipts).

🔵 struggled with balancing being seen vs. being strategic

🔵 wondered how to scale _without_ selling your soul

…this one’s for you. Go give it a watch, take notes, and maybe rewatch again. 🎧 [Listen to the episode here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=i0YK8hi5Vww)

why-mental-health-missing-link-modern-le.title: Why Mental Health Is the Missing Link in Modern Leadership
why-mental-health-missing-link-modern-le.excerpt: Mental Health Isn’t a Buzzword. It’s a Leadership Blueprint We love to talk about innovation, culture, vision, but too many leaders are silent about the one thing that makes it all possible
why-mental-health-missing-link-modern-le.body:
## Mental Health Isn’t a Buzzword. It’s a Leadership Blueprint

We love to talk about innovation, culture, vision, but too many leaders are silent about the one thing that makes it all possible: mental health. May is Mental Health Awareness Month. And let me be real with you, it’s not about vanity metrics or brand-safe statements. It’s about[leadership](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/from-burnout-breakthrough-navigating-stress-leader-joshua-b-lee-j0vlc). Because the most important part of your business walks in the door every day with a full mind and a heavy heart. And if you’re not paying attention to that, you’re not leading. You’re just managing.

> Culture doesn’t break in one big moment; it erodes when we ignore the everyday cracks.

### When It's Personal, It’s Different

Mental health awareness hits different when it’s not a talking point but part of your daily reality. My family has faced some of the hardest versions of this, severe anxiety, depression, PTSD. These aren’t stories from a distance. I’ve seen what it looks like up close. And I’ve felt the helplessness that comes with it.

Living in Texas, raising two teenagers in 2025, this isn’t a trend. It’s a truth. The pressure they face now, the isolation, the performance anxiety, the quiet battles behind those always-on screens, it’s unlike anything we dealt with growing up. And here’s what keeps me up at night: the systems we build as leaders right now are the ones they’ll inherit.My two teens deal with way more in this world than I did as a kid.

This is not fine. For us. For our teams. For our kids. From leadership to culture to everyday life, living in a constant state of mental distress should not be normalized. Unfortunately, this is the reality for [1 in 5](https://www.samhsa.gov/data/sites/default/files/reports/rpt39443/2021NSDUHFFRRev010323.pdf) adults in the US experiencing [mental illness](https://www.thenationalcouncil.org/mental-health-awareness-month/) each year. If your company isn’t mentally healthy, it’s not future-ready, no matter how good the numbers look.

## The Leadership Blind Spot: You Can’t Automate Empathy, But You Can Lead with It

We’ve glamorized hustle culture. Worshipped perfection. And quietly taught our teams that burnout is just the price of ambition. But let’s be honest: most workplace mental health efforts are surface level. A meditation app here. A Slack channel there. Maybe a once-a-year speaker. That’s not a solution. That’s a Band-Aid.

What we really need is a mindset shift: Mental health is infrastructure. It’s the foundation of trust, communication, creativity, everything that makes teams perform at their best. Mindful leadership is now labeled the ultimate corporate advantage. That’s nice, but it’s more than an “edge.” It’s survival. And your people know it. A [Harris poll](https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20250508660090/mental-health-awareness-month-axisharris-poll-survey-finds-nearly-9-in-10-88-insurance-employees-acknowledge-widespread-stress-and-anxiety-in-the-industry) revealed that _nearly 9 in 10 employees report widespread stress and anxiety_ impacting their industries. Here’s what your team actually needs from you:

🔵 Normalize real conversations. When you’re honest, they feel safe to be.

🔵 Build recovery into the system. People aren’t machines, they need cycles of rest, not just grind.

🔵 Train your managers on emotional intelligence. It’s not optional. It’s core leadership.

🔵 Check your incentives. If the only people rewarded are the ones who never stop working, you’re promoting dysfunction.

🔵 Make mental health part of onboarding. Set the tone from day one. This is who we are.

You can’t build a high-performing, happy company on the backs of a stressed-out workforce. It’s like building a house on sand; the cracks will show. The same is true at home for the next generation of leaders. If today’s leaders lack emotional intelligence, what future are we even building?

### The Next Generation is Watching

My kids are watching me. Your team is watching you. And whether you realize it or not, they’re learning what leadership means by how you respond to pressure, vulnerability, and failure. Mental health isn’t just an individual issue, it’s generational. And we’ve got to ask ourselves:

**Are we building a culture that helps our kids, and our teams thrive, or just one that teaches them to survive?**

Because the next wave of leaders isn’t just looking for strategy. They’re looking for spaces where it’s okay to be human. The workplace of the future is being modeled at your dinner table right now.This is my youngest, and I am going to work hard to make sure she lives in a world where it's okay to be human in the workplace.

## My Personal Struggle: When Everything Looked Right, But Felt Wrong

I spent years building businesses that looked like success on paper: High revenue, big impact, massive ad spend numbers that made people say _"wow"._But I was empty, and I was the guy behind the curtain pushing billions of impressions for companies like MySpace and Google and yet I didn’t even feel seen in my own life.

That’s the lie no one warns you about in [entrepreneurship.](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/from-stress-success-4-ways-build-mental-resilience-business-lee-okxvc) The more you chase external validation, the more disconnected you become from your internal reality. I kept pushing. Building. Scaling. Until my first marriage collapsed. Until my body started showing signs of burnout I couldn’t ignore. Until I realized that _balance_ wasn’t just hard, it was a lie.2015 Josh thought he knew better, and now 2025 Josh just wants to hug him and say, we made it out buddy.

That’s why I wrote _Balance is Bullsh_*t, because I needed to tell the truth, I wish someone had told me: That mental health is the foundation of everything, that being _on_ 24/7 is the fastest way to break something that actually matters, that your worth isn’t tied to your calendar or cash flow. And that your people, your team, your family, your future self, need you _present_, not perfect.

> _"I used to think balance was about managing time. What I learned the hard way is that it’s about managing energy, your relationships, your boundaries, and your truth."_— _Balance is Bullsh_*t, Joshua B. Lee

It’s easy to succeed by the world’s standards and still be silently drowning. That’s why I lead with humanity first.

### Where to Start: A Personal Challenge

I’m asking you to move beyond awareness and into action. Not someday. Now. Start by looking in the mirror. What kind of leader are you really?

Here’s how to make mental health a part of your leadership DNA:

🔵 Don’t just say “my door is open.” Walk through theirs.

🔵 Ask, “What’s something you’re carrying that I don’t see?”

🔵 Be okay not having the answers. Sometimes presence is the most powerful solution.

🔵 Share your own story when appropriate. Vulnerability from the top creates space for everyone else.

🔵 Audit your calendar. Are you scheduling burnout or building space for breath?

Your team doesn’t need a superhero. They need a human who gives a damn. Mental health isn’t a marketing message. It’s a leadership imperative. If we want to build businesses that last and leave legacies we’re proud of, we have to get serious about this, not once a year, but every day. Because the culture we create isn’t just a reflection of our values. It’s a roadmap for the people who come next.

* I am not a doctor or a therapist, but if you are suicidal or in emotional distress, consider using the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. Call or text 988 or [start a chat online](https://chat.988lifeline.org/)to connect with a trained crisis counselor. The Lifeline provides 24-hour, confidential support to anyone in suicidal crisis or emotional distress.

## ICYMI 🎙️🎧

One year later and this conversation with [✨ Charles Cormier](https://www.linkedin.com/in/charlescormierfounder?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAABO9_SQBBm1fCiaK3LxRswaRvLptnjKiFLk) on the _CEO Wisdom Podcast_ still lands heavier than ever. Back in 2024, we peeled back the layers on burnout, the illusion of balance, and the mental health realities behind the scenes of building businesses.

That episode still matters today, especially during Mental Health Awareness Month. The hustle hasn’t slowed. Burnout is still real. And the lessons we shared then are more urgent than ever for leaders in 2025.

**Key takeaway that still resonates:**

> “We glorify the grind until it grinds us down. Leadership isn’t about being everywhere at once, it’s about being present where it matters most.”

A huge thank you to Charles Cormier for holding space and leading with candor. One year later, the impact continues and it’s changing the way leaders think and act.

🎧 [Listen to the episode here](https://youtu.be/rOj9V3I2mRY?si=9KJ2cEJ20gcZ914_)

how-use-ai-marketing-without-losing-your.title: How to Use AI in Marketing Without Losing Your Brand Voice
how-use-ai-marketing-without-losing-your.excerpt: AI isn’t killing creativity. It’s just revealing how many people were creating without connection in the first place. Earlier this month, Zuckerberg shared Meta’s new vision: a platform…
how-use-ai-marketing-without-losing-your.body:
AI isn’t killing creativity. It’s just revealing how many people were creating without connection in the first place. Earlier this month, Zuckerberg shared Meta’s new vision: a platform that automates nearly every aspect of content creation. Think full-scale campaigns, creative, copy, targeting, testing, without a single human in the driver’s seat.Photo Source Tekno Sindo News

They’re calling it “[infinite creative](https://www.theverge.com/meta/659506/mark-zuckerberg-ai-facebook-ads).” Sounds like innovation. But if you care about trust, brand, and impact, it should also sound like a warning. I’ve spent two decades helping businesses build massive online visibility. And I’ve never seen a time where clarity of voice and consistency of presence matter more than right now. Here’s what I know: You can automate content. But you cannot automate connection.

I know this because I’ve lived it. Back in the early 2000s, I helped drive nearly a billion dollars in ad spend, scaling platforms like MySpace, Yahoo, and Google before “social strategy” was even a thing. We moved fast, broke records and along the way, I learned what really moves people isn’t volume, it’s value. It’s not how much you say. It’s how true it feels. And in today’s AI-saturated world, that truth, your voice, your presence, is the one thing tech still can’t replicate.

## Scale Is Not Strategy

We’re not short on content. We’re drowning in it. LinkedIn alone has over [1.15 billion](https://www.demandsage.com/linkedin-statistics/) users globally, [230 million](https://www.demandsage.com/linkedin-statistics/) in the U.S.  And now, automation is turning up the volume. Posts, hooks, headlines, all churned out at scale. Feels a lot like the digital version of the Industrial Revolution, just instead of factories, we’ve got content machines.

But here's the thing: volume doesn’t equal value. The more content we create, the more intentional we have to be. Because what captures attention today isn’t just clever, it’s connected. AI can write. It can optimize. But it can’t feel. It doesn’t know your story, your scars, or why you started in the first place. That’s not a gap. That’s your edge.

This isn’t about fighting the rise of AI. It’s about anchoring your voice in the midst of it. When everything starts to sound the same, originality becomes your loudest signal. Especially if you're a founder, consultant, or exec, blending in doesn’t protect your brand, it erases it.Created by DALL-E

Human-led creativity, rooted in lived experience, empathy, and earned insight, isn’t just relevant. It’s rare. And rare wins. Because in a world of mass-produced content, real still resonates.

## What AI Can’t Fake

Let’s call out the illusion: AI promises scale. But what’s sacrificed in the process?

→ Judgment

→ Intuition

→ Empathy

→ Trust

You hand over your voice, and suddenly you're building visibility on someone else’s terms. The algorithm becomes the copywriter, the creative director, and the scorekeeper. And you? You’re just along for the ride. This isn’t a warning about AI. This is a reminder about ownership. When your brand sounds like everyone else, it disappears. When it sounds like you, really you, it cuts through the noise.

## LinkedIn Is Built for the Human Brand

This was never about humans vs. AI. It’s about keeping your voice in a world racing to automate everything. And on LinkedIn? Real still rises. Yes, this is a platform. But more importantly, it’s a place where leaders show up with lived experience. Where perspective matters more than perfection. Where presence is your power move.

Let’s talk content [data](https://www.demandsage.com/linkedin-statistics/)for a second: In 2025, multi-image posts drive a 6.6% engagement rate, the highest of any content format. Native documents and videos aren’t far behind. Meanwhile, text posts and links? Not even close . Why? Because the content that wins here feels like a conversation. Not a campaign.

Multi-image content. Thoughtful comment threads. Strategic conversation. This isn’t performance. It’s participation. And with a 5% average engagement rate by impressions, a number that’s up [30% YoY](https://www.socialinsider.io/social-media-benchmarks/linkedin), it's clear: **connection wins.**

🔵 **Use AI as a tool. Not as your voice.** Let it support the structure. But you drive the soul.

🔵 **Create content that sounds like you.** Real talk. Clear perspective. Shared values. No templates required.

🔵 **Focus on trust metrics.** Measure resonance. DMs. Replies. Relationship depth. That’s your signal.

Meta may be all-in on creative automation. But you? You’ve got the edge they can’t replicate. Your story. Your lived experience. Your POV. Your presence. That’s your competitive advantage. And in a digital sea of sameness, that’s exactly what will make you stand out. Stay human. Stay consistent. Stay loud with your values. Because connection is still the currency and _you_ are still the signal.

## ICYMI 🎙️🎧

If you're ready to cut through the noise and turn your personal brand into a magnet for real opportunities, don’t miss this podcast. I sat down with [Christian Mauerer ♡](https://www.linkedin.com/in/christianmauerer?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAAki8xUBzA8PyHAHGQAEIy9SEhkMySJCcuk) on the _Successful Spiritualpreneur Podcast_ to talk about building authentic brands, the broken influencer mindset, and how AI fits into it all, without losing your human edge.

🎧 [Listen to the episode now](https://open.spotify.com/episode/5cOTOxdlm4JyPaLcq1S80R?si=83440bf748824847)and learn how to show up, stand out, and lead with connection.

from-burnout-breakthrough-navigating-str.excerpt: Stress Isn’t the Enemy, it’s a Messenger. Here we are at the close of April, wrapping up Stress Awareness Month. And if you’ve been navigating the pressure of building a business, leading a
from-burnout-breakthrough-navigating-str.body:
## Stress Isn’t the Enemy, it’s a Messenger.

Here we are at the close of April, wrapping up Stress Awareness Month. And if you’ve been navigating the pressure of building a business, leading a team, or simply showing up each day with intention, you’re not alone.

This isn’t a moment for confetti. It’s a moment for reflection. Because for those of us integrating ambition with authenticity, stress isn’t just noise, it’s a signal. And how we choose to listen to it makes all the difference.

Let’s rewind. There was a chapter of my life where the “American dream” turned into a damn near burnout reel. I was living in my parents' basement (yep, as a grown man), tanked one business deal that lost $1.3 million, watched $9 million walk out the door in another, and let’s just say my nervous system was fried.Me circa 2014, if you would have told this guy what was to come, he wouldn’t have believed you.

But here’s the kicker: I didn’t crash because I failed. I crashed because I was hustling with _zero alignment_. That’s the kind of stress that doesn't just keep you up at night, it rewires your soul. It makes you question if all the emails, all the intense long hour days, and all the pitch decks are worth the cost.

## The Numbers Are Real and They’re Not Pretty

👊 Workplace stress has been [reported](https://www.osha.gov/workplace-stress#ref3) to cause 120,000 deaths in the US each year

👊 Life expectancy for [men in the U.S](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products/databriefs/db521.htm). is still down from pre-pandemic highs

👊Millennials and Gen Z are clocking in with [lower health scores](https://mhanational.org/2024-workplace-wellness-research/) than older generations

Translation: we’re not just burned out; we’re biologically paying the price. But the problem isn’t stress itself. It’s how we respond to it. Let me say it louder for the high performers in the back: **Stress isn’t here to ruin you. It’s here to redirect you.**

The stress you feel is often a symptom of 3 core things:
- Misalignment: You’re chasing “shoulds,” not your own purpose.
- Isolation: You’re doing it all alone and pretending you’re fine.
- Over-identification: You _are_ your business. If it fails, you think you fail.

I’ve lived every single one of those. Hell, sometimes I still do. But now I’ve got the tools to catch myself before I spiral.

## Health Is More Than a Side Hustle, It’s Your Leadership Foundation

One of the hardest lessons I’ve learned as a founder wasn’t about scaling companies or closing big deals. It was this: you can’t outperform a body and mind running on fumes. Years ago, I was grinding so hard I couldn’t walk up a flight of stairs without getting winded. I was leading multiple businesses, but I wasn’t leading _myself_. And honestly? Everything around me, my clarity, my energy, even my joy, was out of shape.Circa 2015, I thought hustle culture was the answer, I learned the hard way it wasn’t.

That wake-up call forced me to shift. Not with some massive overhaul, but with small, intentional changes:
- A 10-minute walk to reset my brain.
- Fueling with better food so I could actually think clearly.
- Journaling when my thoughts started spiraling.

Those little tweaks? They added up. And they created the kind of capacity I needed to lead, not just _do more_, but _be more present_ for my team, my clients, and most importantly, myself.

> The truth is that health isn’t a reward for getting through the stress, it’s the foundation that lets you rise above it.

When you make space for your mental, emotional, and physical well-being, you’re not stepping back from leadership. You’re stepping _into_ the kind of leadership that lasts. So, if you’re feeling the pressure right now, ask yourself: _Where can I lead from care, not just grind?_Because when your health becomes your baseline, _everything_ else, your business, your vision, your relationships, levels up with you.

## Build a Life That Can Hold What You’re Building

Most of us spend so much time building businesses, chasing opportunities, and stacking calendars… We forget to build a life that can actually _hold_ the success we’re aiming for. Stress shows up when the system we are operating in, mentally, emotionally, even physically, can’t meet the moment we’re in.

And I get it. I’ve been there. I’ve built fast, lost fast, and learned the hard way that _growth without grounding is just a faster way to burn out._So now? My goal isn’t just to grow, it’s to grow _with capacity._Graphic by DALL-E

Here’s how I define leadership capacity:
- Mental bandwidth to solve big problems without spiraling into burnout.
- Emotional regulation so I can lead with clarity, not reactivity.
- Nervous system resilience so I can show up, even when the pressure’s real.

The entrepreneurs and execs who will win in this next chapter aren’t the ones who hustle harder. They’re the ones who can _hold more_, without losing themselves in the process. If that’s the game you want to play, ask yourself: What am I building right now that supports my _life_, not just my business? That’s where leadership gets real. That’s how stress becomes a catalyst, not a curse. Stay grounded, stay real, and stress just might become your superpower.

## Mental Resilience Is the New ROI

Here’s something I’ve learned the hard way: your title might say “Founder,” “CEO,” or “Executive,” but stress doesn’t care. It hits all of us. And if you’re leading without prioritizing your mental health, you're leading on borrowed time. We talk a lot about _mindset_ in business, growth mindset, strategic mindset, performance mindset. But the one that often gets overlooked? **Resilience.**

Not the “push through it” kind. The kind that helps you respond instead of react. The kind that allows you to make hard calls without hardening your heart. Here’s why it matters now more than ever: A [2024 study](https://www.forbes.com/sites/bryanrobinson/2024/04/15/number-1-reason-managers-have-a-bigger-mental-health-impact-than-your-therapist/) revealed nearly **70% of employees** say their manager impacts their mental health more than their doctor or therapist. That’s wild. That’s also equal to the impact of a romantic partner. I’ve come along way, and I am still learning, I'll always be evolving, but I now know more than anything, it's my famiLEE that comes first above everything else.

So, let’s be clear, leadership isn’t just about direction. It’s about emotional influence. The way you show up sets the tone. This isn’t about being perfect. It’s about being present. It’s about creating cultures where performance doesn’t come at the cost of well-being. Empathy scales trust. Resilience scales leadership. And if you’ve been treating mental health like a checkbox, maybe it’s time to treat it like your next big growth strategy.

### 🔁 ICYMI: A Human-First Fireside Chat on AI That Hit Different

Wow. That fireside chat was one for the books. If you joined us live last week, thank you. We know time is one of your most valuable currencies, and the fact that you spent an hour with us means the world.

Big shoutout to [John Stix](https://www.linkedin.com/in/johnstix?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAACrVKcBV2TDTYSftyLt5QokTDBJSq4gnR0) , who dropped pure gold on how small businesses can scale with AI _without losing the human edge_. His insights on ethical innovation and real-world application? Game-changing. And of course, a huge thanks to [Rachel B. Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/therachelblee?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAATthuAB-Gy4FMm8KnvDftaFczqyPAUOIsI) for helping guide a conversation that wasn’t just smart, it was real.

Couldn’t make it? We got you. 👉 [Catch the replay here](https://vimeo.com/1078067665)

This wasn’t theory. It was strategy, lived experience, and next steps you can act on now.

lead-your-voice-algorithms-heres-how-sta.body:
## AI Can’t Fake Trust and Your Audience Knows It

### Why Real Leaders Still Win in the Age of Automation

Look, I love AI. You know that. I’ve been playing with it since before most people knew what a prompt was. But here’s the thing no one’s saying out loud... If you’re outsourcing your voice to AI, you’re already losing. Because leadership? Influence? Trust? That still needs a human behind the curtain. It’s not just about showing up online. It’s about how you show up. And too many smart, powerful people are fading into the noise right now, posting “good enough” content made by machines, crossing their fingers, and wondering why no one’s engaging anymore.

Let me make it plain: [AI is a tool. YOU are the message.](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/why-best-leaders-use-content-spark-conversations-just-joshua-b-lee-lvyvc?trackingId=Xo18ZGsmSlGRgkmcYUVK7Q%3D%3D&lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Ad_flagship3_profile_view_base_recent_activity_content_view%3BVn4ODZULRnCKRjki2amnhQ%3D%3D)

### Automation Isn’t the Enemy, but Absence Is

We’re living in a wild time. Content is everywhere. AI can write blog posts, generate videos, even clone your voice (ask me how I know 😉). But here's the truth most people won’t tell you: If you’re not intentionally leading with your values, your vision, and your actual VOICE ... AI will start to do it for you**.**And not in a good way.

Your audience doesn’t want polish. They want presence. They want real. They want YOU. According to a [Forbes article](https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbesbusinesscouncil/2025/04/07/series-a-and-beyond-essential-lessons-for-founders-entering-the-growth-phase/), “The key is to use AI to enhance, not replace, your brand’s voice”.  And I know how tempting it is to plug your stuff into a tool and let it do the heavy lifting. I’ve done it. I’ve experimented with it. But the content that hits hardest? It’s still the unscripted, straight-from-the-heart stuff I film in my car between school pickup or walking the dogs and baby.

Because trust isn’t built by bots. It’s built by leaders who show up, even when they don’t have a script.

## So, How Do You Stay Human in a High-Tech World?

Here’s what we teach at [StandOut Authority](https://www.linkedin.com/company/standoutauthority/), and what Rachel and I practice every single day with our clients, our team, and yep, even when it’s just the two of us at the kitchen counter working through strategy.

### 1️⃣ Lead with Stories, Not Stats

Data is helpful. Stories are unforgettable. Want to connect? Share something real. A win, a mistake, a lesson that cost you something, but made you better. That’s what people lean into.

_Reminder: The human_🧠 _brain is wired for story, not bullet points._

### 2️⃣ Quality > Noise

Posting every day doesn’t mean anything if it all sounds the same. You want connection? Stop posting to check a box. Start posting to spark a conversation. Ask yourself: “Would I stop scrolling to read this?” If the answer’s no, don’t publish. Rework it until it’s unmistakably yours.

### 3️⃣ Trust Isn’t a Metric. It’s a Feeling

According to [PwC’s 2024 Trust Survey](https://www.pwc.com/us/en/library/trust-in-business-survey/customer-trust-in-your-sector.html), 91% of people say they’re more likely to buy from brands they trust. But trust isn’t something you _get._ It’s something you _earn._You earn it when you…
- Reply to comments with intention
- Show up consistently without chasing virality
- Say the thing no one else is saying, even when it’s uncomfortable

That’s how you lead. And that’s how you scale. With or without AI.

## Your Face Beats Any Fancy Logo

People don’t follow brands. They follow humans who know who they are, what they stand for, and who aren’t afraid to show up, unfiltered and real. That’s you. Or at least, it should be. And if you’ve been posting content that looks good but feels flat, here’s your permission slip to stop. Ditch the template. Drop the perfectionism. Lead with your damn voice, even if someone doesn’t like it or wants to rip you apart.

I recently had this happen to me, I posted a [video with my POV](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuablee_jobmarket-careergrowth-workforcetrends-activity-7307506044245590016-ZX6t?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAApciIMByUxTZ0oDjJenExsOWihjaHVGITQ)on LinkedIn and it upset someone enough that they made a [YouTube video on me](https://youtu.be/8k1S-mf51S4?si=1dJgMHeVeMj0zwTr)🤪 If your content is meant to spark conversation, and it should be, it’s not going to align with everyone. And that’s a good thing.

When we lead with our values and lived experiences, not hate, not noise, we create space for real dialogue. So, if someone disagrees with your perspective and shares their take in the comments or makes an entire YouTube video about you 😝… That’s not a problem. That’s the point. I’m not here to be universally liked and neither should you. I’m here to be real, lead with intention, and build a community that knows how to talk, not just scroll.

Because at the end of the day, people don’t follow perfection, they follow presence. They follow the ones who show up consistently. Who lead with their voice, not just their tools. Who aren’t afraid to be real in a world that’s becoming increasingly automated.

> So, the question isn’t _“How do I keep up with AI?”_ It’s _“How do I lead with more humanity as I grow with it?”_

That’s where trust lives. That’s where leadership lives. And that’s the edge no algorithm can replicate. Let’s keep building it, one real connection at a time. 👊

## Ready to Talk About the Real Stuff?

[Wednesday April 23rd](https://www.linkedin.com/events/aican-tfaketrust-howtoscalewith7312887041388658688/about/), I’m sitting down for a 🔥 fireside chat with two of my favorite humans, [Rachel B. Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/therachelblee?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAATthuAB-Gy4FMm8KnvDftaFczqyPAUOIsI) and [John Stix](https://www.linkedin.com/in/johnstix?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAACrVKcBV2TDTYSftyLt5QokTDBJSq4gnR0) from Nucleus AI. We’re breaking down:
- How to use AI _without_ losing your humanity
- Why your personal brand is your most valuable business asset in 2025
- What trust actually looks like (and how to earn it at scale)

Oh, and we’re giving away a FREE AI Employee, courtesy of Nucleus AI. Yep. An AI team member. That’s happening. [Reserve your spot](https://www.linkedin.com/events/aican-tfaketrust-howtoscalewith7312887041388658688/about/) 📌

Leadership in this new era isn’t about being perfect. It’s about being present. The people who win online and offline are the ones who know how to integrate the tech, without losing the heart.

why-best-leaders-use-content-spark-conve.body:
## Content Isn’t King, QUALITY CONTENT IS QUEEN

You ever sit down to watch something on Netflix and spend more time scrolling than actually watching? Yeah, that’s exactly what content feels like right now. Too many options. Too much noise. And the more we scroll, the less we actually care. We don’t act, we check out.DALL-E depicted what this would look like.

People aren’t short on content, they’re short on clarity. They’re overloaded, distracted, and numb to anything that doesn’t spark connection or value. So if your content isn’t creating movement, it’s just background noise. Let’s shift that.

### Influence Without Action Is Just Noise

I’m not here to be some influencer chasing likes. That’s not the goal. Vanity metrics don’t pay the bills. And they definitely don’t build trust. What I do care about, and what we do every day at StandOut Authority, is helping you build a presence that actually moves people. Not just to think, but to do something.

Because here’s the truth: if your content isn’t sparking action, it’s just noise with better lighting. Algorithms are evolving. Audiences are sharper. People can sniff out fluff from a mile away. So if you’re not showing up with real value? They’re not showing up for you. Simple as that. You don’t need to post more; you need to post better.

### Real Content With Real Purpose.

Here’s what I see working right now with top leaders and creators on LinkedIn and what we teach and practice ourselves:

🔵**Stop Posting Just to Post**

If you're pushing out content just to stay “visible,” you're wasting time. A [Forbes article](https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbesbusinesscouncil/2025/03/20/18-strategies-for-maintaining-company-culture-amid-a-generational-shift/) confirms it: personalization is key. Quality content, created for the right audience, cuts through. Less volume. More meaning.

🔵 **Create Conversations That Move People**

Content that makes people think is good. Content that makes people act is better. When I started asking questions in my posts that hit a nerve, like, “What’s the hardest leadership lesson you’ve learned?” my inbox lit up. Not because I was pushing. But because I was connecting.

🔵**Quality > Quantity**

A [Gartner report](https://www.gartner.com/en/documents/5026531) shows consumers are actively pulling back from platforms due to declining content quality. This is your opportunity. Don’t try to be everywhere. Be effective where it counts.

🔵 **Double Down on Human Connection**

Algorithms shift. People stay. The real strategy? Get human. Comment meaningfully. DM with intent. Show up in other people’s worlds before you ask them to enter yours. That’s how influence is built.

And let’s not ignore the facts. If you’re in the B2B space, LinkedIn is the arena. About [40% of B2B marketers](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/audience) say LinkedIn is their most effective lead gen channel, because the platform gives you direct access to decision-makers, high-quality buyers, and partners who are already in a business mindset.

But here’s the catch: showing up just to post isn’t what works. Showing up with clarity, consistency, and real human value? That’s what gets you seen, and remembered.

## Your Personal Brand > Company Logo

People don’t want to connect with companies. They want to connect with you. Your story. Your voice. Your values. Your content doesn’t need to be “perfect.” It needs to be personal and purpose-driven. Here’s what backs it all up, media content is one of the biggest trust signals for consumers today. That’s not just me talking. That’s straight from the latest [Salsify Consumer Trust Report.](https://www.salsify.com/blog/why-brand-trust-makes-shoppers-pay-more) People aren’t just watching what you post, they’re deciding if they trust you because of it.

So I’ll ask you this, if your content were a product, would your audience buy it?Salsify 2025 Consumer Research Report about consumer trust proves to me that digital media is where MOST of the connection between people, brands, and audiences happens.

## Forget Playing the Game; Start Owning Your Space

You don’t stand out online by shouting the loudest or posting the most. You do it by showing up with purpose. It’s not about being everywhere; it’s about being remembered for something that matters. I like to keep things real, simple, and actionable. So here are 3 ways I consistently show up with intention, and how you can too.

### ✅ Play the 5x Rule

Want people to notice you? Start paying attention to them first. Comment thoughtfully on five posts before you even think about posting your own. The more you show up for others the more they will show up for you. It’s basically like an unspoken digital pledge.It takes less than 15 minutes to comment thoughtfully on 5 posts before you even think about posting your own.

### ✅ Post With Purpose

Your next post shouldn’t be fluff. No generic “Motivational Monday” quotes. Instead, share something real. A bold opinion. A lesson that shaped you. Something that happened that taught you a valuable life or business lesson. According to Simon Simek (an entrepreneur I highly admire), to [hook your audience in 30 seconds](https://simonsinek.com/stories/how-to-hook-your-audience-in-30-seconds-according-to-simon/) or less, it’s important to include storytelling in your content. The story gives your content purpose, which your audience will find reassuring.

Here’s what’s wild: [77% of marketers say LinkedIn gives them the best organic results](https://blog.hootsuite.com/linkedin-statistics/) out of any platform. Not TikTok. Not Insta. Not SEO wizardry that takes six months to maybe work. Just showing up with real content on the platform where people actually come to think, lead, and make business happen. But let’s be clear: those results don’t come from surface-level posts.

They come from knowing your audience, speaking their language, and showing up consistently with content that hits.

### ✅ Lead By Example

Want better engagement? Don’t beg for it. Create it. Meaningful conversations start, not with a “please engage,” but with your willingness to show up consistently. I see this in my own team, when I show up authentically, my team becomes more active on the same platforms. So you’re not just influencing your audience; you’re sharing your entire network.

## Your Next Post Is a Moment, Make It Count

Content isn’t just a marketing play. It’s your leadership in public. If you’re showing up with real intent, building relationships, and focusing on value, not volume, you’re already doing more than most.

What’s one small shift you can make this week to create an actual connection, not just another post in the feed? Because, let’s be real, the internet isn’t starving for more content. But it is starving for more people who show up with something real to say.

👉 And if this hit a nerve, if you’re a leader in the corporate world or building a brand that’s tired of posting without traction, DM me. Let’s talk about how Standout Authority can help you create content that actually connects, converts, and means something. No pitch. Just a real conversation.

strategic-ai-advantage-building-linkedin.body:
## From Noise to Signal: A Tale of Two Approaches

Recently, while scrolling through LinkedIn, I encountered two posts about leveraging AI for business growth. One was clearly AI-generated, filled with generic advice and corporate jargon. The other had a genuine human touch, sharing a specific challenge, the author's approach to overcoming it using AI, and the lessons learned.DALLE Graphic Depicting A Tale of Two Approaches

The difference was impossible to ignore, and it speaks to a bigger choice we all face on LinkedIn. Some people treat AI like a shortcut, cranking out generic posts and hoping volume somehow turns into value. But the real ones? They use AI as a tool to sharpen their voice, not replace it. They lean into their expertise, their stories, and their humanity, AI just helps them do it better.

I know which path I'm taking. Here's why.

## The Strategic AI Framework: Lessons from the Front Lines

When I first experimented with AI for my LinkedIn strategy, I made numerous mistakes. I attempted to automate everything, believing technology could handle it all. My engagement plummeted, and a long-time connection even asked, "Are you okay? Your posts don't sound like you anymore."

That was my wake-up call. Since then, I've refined an approach that enhances, rather than replaces, meaningful connections. Here's what I've learned:

### 1. Data-Driven Storytelling: Finding the Balance

Think about the last time a story truly captivated you. It wasn't just the facts, it was the presentation, the emotional journey, those moments of recognition where you thought, "Yes, that's exactly how it feels!"

AI can't replicate that. However, it can assist in other ways. Last month, I was wrestling with how to break down a complex industry trend. I knew what I wanted to say, but I just couldn't find the right way to frame it. So, I put AI to work, analyzing top-performing posts on similar topics, spotting patterns in how people were structuring their ideas, and dialing in the best format and length to make it land.

The result? One of my most engaged posts this year. The story, examples, and voice remained uniquely mine.

### 2. Relationship Intelligence: The Coffee Shop Approach

Imagine your LinkedIn network as a bustling coffee shop. Some are just passing through, others are regulars who always say hello, and some are potential collaborators awaiting the right conversation. Without a system, it's chaotic. You might try to engage with everyone (connecting with no one) or miss opportunities because you didn't notice someone trying to catch your eye.

That's where my "☕Coffee Shop AI System" comes in.

I've developed a simple tracking system to identify who consistently engages with my content, who has visited my profile multiple times, and who leaves thoughtful comments rather than generic praise.

Recently, this system highlighted someone who had engaged with three of my posts about data analytics but hadn't reached out directly. I sent a personalized message acknowledging their insights, and we're now discussing a potential collaboration that might have otherwise been overlooked. DALLE Graphic Depicting 3 Lessons from The Frontline

### 3. Systems vs. Relationships: What I Automate (And What I Don't)

Confession: For three weeks, I used a fully automated messaging system. The results were disastrous. Conversations felt stilted, opportunities fizzled, and I damaged a few relationships I'd spent months building. Now, I follow a simple rule: Automate tasks that don't require human judgment and personally handle those that do.

_I use AI to: _

🔵Draft initial content outlines based on topics my audience engages with

🔵Suggest optimal posting times based on my engagement history

🔵Track relationship stages and remind me when to follow up

_But I personally handle: _

👊Refining my voice and storytelling in every piece of content

👊Responding to comments with genuine curiosity and care

👊Building relationships through authentic conversations

The difference is profound. My engagement has increased, but more importantly, the quality of my connections has deepened significantly.

## The 2025 LinkedIn Authority Report: A Sneak Peek

I've been documenting my journey and analyzing the strategies of the most effective LinkedIn voices I know. The result is a comprehensive guide I'm calling "The Strategic AI Advantage: LinkedIn Authority in 2025."

Here's a story that illustrates just one insight from the report:

One of my clients, a financial advisor with decades of expertise but minimal LinkedIn presence, was reluctant to embrace AI. "It just isn't authentic," she told me. Instead of pushing technology, we started with story structure. We identified her most impactful client transformations and created templates that preserved her voice while making content creation more efficient. Six months later, her engagement increased by 287%, and more importantly, she generated 12 qualified leads directly from LinkedIn, something that had never happened before.

The report contains dozens of similar case studies, along with specific frameworks you can implement immediately.

📢 **Want early access? Reply to this newsletter with "AI Report" and share one challenge you're currently facing with your LinkedIn presence.** I'll personally ensure you receive the report next week along with a customized suggestion for your specific situation.

## The Path Forward: Where Will You Walk?

A few days ago, I was having coffee with a colleague who asked me, "Do you really think AI is worth all this effort? Couldn't we just keep doing things the old way?" I thought about it for a moment, then asked: "Remember when social media first emerged, and some professionals insisted it was just a fad? Where are they now?" The question isn't whether to use AI in your LinkedIn strategy, it's how thoughtfully you implement it to enhance what already makes you valuable. DALLE Graphic Depicting the Path Forward, but notice the errors, your humanness is irreplaceable.

This week, I challenge you to look at one piece of content you're planning to share. Before you post it, ask yourself:

🔵Does this sound like me at my best?

🔵Does it share a story only I could tell?

🔵Does it provide value only I could offer?

If not, it might be time to tweak your approach. I'd love to hear your thoughts. What's one way you've used technology to enhance rather than replace your authentic voice?

_This edition of my Dopamine Dose newsletter is part of my ongoing story of navigating the intersection of technology and human connection. If you found it valuable, I'd appreciate you sharing it with others on a similar journey._

your-linkedin-strategy-missing-one.body:
## More Views, More Comments, More Conversations—This Is the Missing Piece

Does LinkedIn feel quieter to you lately? The posts keep coming, but the magic, the real conversations, debates, and _aha_ moments, feels like it’s on life support.

You used to scroll through your feed and actually _learn_ something. Now? It’s like walking into a networking event where everyone’s staring at their phones, waiting for someone else to start talking first.AI created this graphic, hence the spelling being wrong. But you get the point.

Here’s what happened:

❌ **Content Overload** – The average person consumes 7+ hours of digital media per day reported by [Statista](https://www.statista.com/topics/1536/media-use/#topicOverview). No wonder we’re all tuning out—the noise is deafening.

❌ **Engagement Isn’t What It Used to Be** – Even though the average LinkedIn post is seeing more engagements than last year according to [Statista,](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1483853/linkedin-posts-average-engagement/) overall interaction rates are dropping across social media. People are scrolling more, engaging less.

## LinkedIn Isn’t Broken—People Just Forgot How to Connect

If you want engagement, you don’t need a growth hack (_gross_) 🤮. You need _human connection_. People have to remember there’s a real person on the other side of that post.

Here’s what works—and why it’s worth sticking with it:

🔵 **Write for humans, not robots.** If your post sounds like a corporate press release, nobody cares. Ask yourself: _Would I say this in a real conversation?_

🔵 **Ask better questions.** Not “What’s your favorite leadership book?”—but “What’s the biggest leadership mistake you’ve ever made, and what did you learn from it?” Give people something _worth_ responding to.

🔵 **Get off autopilot.** Someone takes the time to comment? Don’t just hit “Like.” Reply. Ask them something back. Engagement isn’t a one-way street.

**Pro Tip:** The people who create conversations are the ones who get remembered.

## Less Noise, More Impact: A 3-Step Fix for Meaningful Engagement

I know what you’re thinking—“Sounds great, but how do I actually _do_ this?” Glad you asked.

Here’s your roadmap for the week ahead.

✅ **1. The 5x Rule:** Comment on five posts per day before posting your own. Why? Because engagement is a two-way street. If you want people to notice your posts, start by showing up in their conversations.

✅ **2. Purposeful Posting:** Share a story, a lesson, or a strong opinion—no fluffy “Monday Motivation” quotes. Give people something to respond to.

✅ **3. Lead by Doing:** If you want engagement, don’t beg for it—create it. The best posts don’t just get likes; they _start movements._

**Why does this matter?** [PwC](https://www.pwc.com/us/trustsurvey)found that when leaders show up _authentically_ online, their teams are 72% more likely to engage on those same platforms.

This isn’t just about _your_ engagement—it’s about the ripple effect you create.

## The Best Leaders Don’t Just Post. They Start Conversations

Leaders aren’t remembered for the posts they _scheduled_—they’re remembered for the conversations they _started._If LinkedIn feels dead, don’t wait for someone else to revive it.

Be the person who _asks the real questions_. The one who _challenges the status quo_. The one who _actually shows up_. Because at the end of the day, social media is what you make of it.

Treat LinkedIn like a dumping ground for generic content, and that’s exactly what you’ll get back. But treat it like a **human connection machine**—and you’ll build something people _can’t stop talking about._Source Credit Sir Richard Branson LinkedIn

Richard Branson isn’t just a business mogul—he’s a master of conversation.

Scroll through his LinkedIn, and you won’t just see corporate updates or polished PR statements. You’ll see stories. Questions. Personal reflections that invite real dialogue.

Whether he’s sharing lessons from his failures, debating the future of business, or championing causes he believes in, Branson doesn’t just post—he _engages_. And that’s why people don’t just _follow_ him. They _talk_ to him.

_That’s the difference._

## Stop Waiting for Conversations. Start Creating Them

🔵 **Engage on five posts today.** Thoughtful comments only—_no fluff._

🔵 **Write one post this week** that invites conversation—something raw, real, and worth responding to.

🔵 **Reply to every single comment you get.** Because conversations build connections—and connections build opportunities.

This isn’t about _playing the LinkedIn game._ It’s about _leading the conversation._And trust me—the people who do that? They’re not just noticed. They’re _remembered._

👊 **Your move.**

your-linkedin-profile-talking-saying-rig.excerpt: LinkedIn Isn’t a Chore—It’s Your Digital Reputation Most people treat LinkedIn like a to-do list item—something they “have to” post on, optimize, or engage with. But here’s the reality: Lin
your-linkedin-profile-talking-saying-rig.body:
## LinkedIn Isn’t a Chore—It’s Your Digital Reputation

Most people treat LinkedIn like a to-do list item—something they “have to” post on, optimize, or engage with. But here’s the reality: LinkedIn is shaping your reputation whether you’re active or not. Every comment, post, and interaction (or lack of one) is building your digital presence. The question is—are you letting it happen by accident, or are you being intentional?

I’ve been a LinkedIn member since 2006, and I’ve spent years helping leaders, founders, and brands build real influence on this platform. And what I’ve seen? The people who stand out aren’t following a magic formula. They’re just showing up with purpose, staying human, and playing the long game.

Here’s how you actually own your space on LinkedIn and stand out.LinkedIn does not have to be complicated.

## Your Profile = Your First Impression

Your profile isn’t a business card—it’s your reputation at scale.

If someone lands on your page and doesn’t instantly understand who you are and why you matter, they’re gone.My Current LinkedIn Profile

✅ **Headline:** Skip the job title. This is your hook. Make it clear, compelling, and human.

**Example:** Instead of _“Marketing Director | Speaker | Consultant”_, try “Helping businesses simplify their message and grow through clear, compelling marketing”—this tells people _what you do_ and _why it matters,_and then add a few title items.

✅ **About Section:** If your ‘About’ sounds like a corporate press release, rewrite it. Tell people _why_ you do what you do.

**Example:** Instead of _“Experienced executive with a background in SaaS and business development”_, try something that actually connects:  _"I believe sales isn’t about pushing products—it’s about solving problems. After 15 years in SaaS, I’ve learned that the best deals come from conversations, not cold pitches. My mission? Helping teams shift from selling to serving."_

This works because it tells a story, builds credibility, and reinforces a core belief—without sounding like a résumé.

✅ **Profile Photo & Banner:** People connect with faces, not logos. And if your banner isn’t reinforcing your message, you’re wasting space.

**Example:** Instead of a generic city skyline or a stock image, use a banner that tells people what you stand for—like a clear value statement, a photo of you speaking, or a tagline that reinforces your expertise.

Profiles with strong summaries and high-quality images get[21x more views](https://www.socialinsider.io/social-media-benchmarks/linkedin). Read your LinkedIn summary out loud. If it sounds robotic, fix it. If it doesn’t sound like something you’d say in a real conversation, rewrite it until it does. Make your profile a magnet—not a missed opportunity.

## Content That Actually Feels Like You

The fastest way to get ignored? Post content that sounds like everyone else.

The fastest way to get noticed? Post content that sounds like YOU.

What works?

🔵 Stories that teach a lesson. Not just “here’s what happened,” but “here’s what I learned.”

🔵 Hot takes that spark conversation. Say what others are afraid to say—but back it up.

🔵 Behind-the-scenes moments. People don’t just want to see your wins—they want to see your process, failures, and growth.

**Bonus Tip:**Video is your secret weapon. Forget polished, overproduced nonsense. Grab your phone, hit record, and speak directly to your audience.Not bad for a video post on a trending LinkedIn News story. Check it out below.

LinkedIn video views are up [36%](https://www.socialinsider.io/social-media-benchmarks/linkedin) year-over-year, and 75% of U.S. adults spend up to two hours a day watching short-form video. Post something this week that actually sounds like you—not a watered-down, corporate version of you.

## Engagement = The Real Differentiator

If you’re just posting and running, you’re missing the point. LinkedIn isn’t a stage—it’s a conversation.

**How to engage like a pro:**

✅ Comment on 5-10 posts a day—but actually add value.****

✅ DM people when their content resonates with you. Start real convos.

✅ Reply to every comment on your posts—because trust is built in the replies.

Stop lurking. Engage on 5 posts today with real, thoughtful comments. Watch what happens.Wolverine Illustration Credit Screen Rant

## The Bottom Line: Presence Over Perfection

Owning your space on LinkedIn isn’t about being everywhere, doing everything, or chasing algorithms. It’s about being **intentional, consistent, and real.**

✅ Optimize your profile so people get who you are at a glance.

✅ Post content that makes people stop scrolling.

✅ Engage like you actually care.

That’s it. Do this consistently, and you won’t just get noticed—you’ll get remembered. Now, what’s one thing you’re shifting in your LinkedIn strategy this week? Drop it in the comments. Let’s talk.

### A Quick Favor (If You’ve Got 30 Seconds 🙏)

I’ve been nominated for a Texas Creator Award—which means our mission of making LinkedIn more real, more human, and more valuable is getting the recognition it deserves.

If you’ve ever found value in what I share, I’d love your support.

➡️  [Click HERE to vote](https://texascreatorawards.com/vote/) **for me in the LinkedIn Articles and Posts Category. **

Thanks, famiLEE. Let’s keep making LinkedIn the most human place online. 👊

how-stop-being-invisible-use-linkedin-ow.body:
## Stop Hiding: LinkedIn Is Your Stage, Google Is Your Spotlight

Let’s get something straight: If you’re not showing up online, you’re not in the game. Period.

Right now, as the digital world feels noisier and messier than ever, LinkedIn stands out as the last truly [human platform](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/one-simple-strategy-took-my-linkedin-from-zero-hero-joshua-b-lee-4ycqc/?trackingId=jR%2F0affoT32AOIqXbOJk4Q%3D%3D), a space that values connection over clout, conversations over clicks, and real leadership over recycled trends.

LinkedIn isn’t just a platform, it’s Google’s goldmine. Every post you write, every comment you drop, and every profile update you make? It’s indexed and searchable. Your LinkedIn presence isn’t just for today’s feed; it’s building your long-term discoverability across the web.

So, ask yourself: Are you even in the game if Google doesn’t know you exist?

## The Truth About LinkedIn: It’s the Web’s Most Underrated Asset

Here’s some context for you. Google just dropped the top searches of 2024:
- U.S. election
- Extreme heat weather
- Paris Olympics

Big topics. But here’s the deal: If your name, your brand, or your expertise isn’t showing up alongside the conversations that matter, you’re irrelevant.

LinkedIn gives you the power to change that. Every interaction, post, comment, and article contributes to your personal SEO. This is how you become discoverable, not just on LinkedIn but across the entire digital landscape.

💡 **Pro Tip:**Start using LinkedIn’s trending news sidebar (that little box on the right-hand side of your dashboard). If something aligns with your perspective or expertise, create a quick post or video that adds value. The goal isn’t just visibility; it’s credibility._Check the right hand side of your LinkedIn dashboard and join the conversation. _

## My Latest Experiment: Making the LinkedIn Trending News a Priority

For the past few weeks, I’ve been trying a new approach: creating quick, real-time content based on trending news. I focus on stories that connect with my pillars, like leadership, connection, and innovation, or simply topics that grab my attention and spark a genuine opinion because I care about it.

### The Data Doesn’t Lie: A Closer Look at the Analytics

To give you some perspective on this experiment, here are my top-performing posts over the last 14 and 28 days, based on both impressions and engagement:

📈 **In the last 14 days:**
- - Meta’s Bold AI Move: 1.5M+ impressions, 181 comments, and a flood of conversations about what this means for leaders navigating AI.
- - Red Dye #3: Fewer impressions (396,000+) but _real_ conversations with 86 comments from people genuinely engaging with the topic.
- - TikTok & Digital Control: This quick, lighthearted post hit 800,000+ impressions, proving that humor and a sharp take can still generate serious reach.

📊**In the last 28 days:** Across all posts, I’ve seen a 64.6% increase in engagement, reaching over 4,400 engagements.

> It’s not just about what’s trending, it’s about _how_ you show up. Are you sharing a genuine POV, or are you just checking the content box?

### Why This Experiment Matters to You

Here’s what these numbers and conversations are teaching me, and hopefully, they’ll resonate with you too:

🔵Visibility Is Step One: If you’re not part of the conversation, you’re invisible. LinkedIn and Google are where the digital world connects.

🔵Engagement Is Step Two: People want to engage with your mind, not just your content. Dive into the comments, ask questions, and build trust one interaction at a time.

🔵Consistency Wins the Game: You don’t have to post daily, but you do need to show up intentionally. Align your voice with your audience’s needs, and don’t be afraid to take a stance.

🔑 Key Takeaway: Stop overthinking your content. It’s not about perfection; it’s about presence. Even small, authentic contributions can open big doors.

### My Challenge to You

Take a page from my playbook and try this for the next three weeks:

1️⃣ Check LinkedIn’s trending news daily. What aligns with your brand pillars or personal interests?

2️⃣ Post something quick and real. A short video, a sharp take, or a simple question can spark meaningful conversations.

3️⃣ Engage in the comments. Don’t just post and ghost. The magic happens when you dive into the discussions.

**But here’s the catch:** Your audience knows you. If you go off-topic or chase trends that don’t align with your pillars, they’ll see right through it. Stay in your lane, but don’t be afraid to bring fresh perspectives and authentic takes.

_Remember:_ The numbers might get you noticed, but it’s the conversations that build trust, relationships, and opportunities.

## Personal SEO is Non-Negotiable

If someone Googles you and finds nothing, you’re invisible.

LinkedIn is Google’s vault for your personal brand. Every post, every comment, every headline, it’s all indexed. And if you’re not intentional about how you show up, someone else will define your narrative for you. When people search for you, they’re not just looking for your job title, they’re looking for your story, your perspective, and what you stand for.

🔵 Optimize Your Profile: Make your headline more than just a title, make it a statement of value.

🔵 Post Weekly: Align your content with topics that matter to you AND your audience.

🔵 Engage Thoughtfully: Don’t just drop emojis in comments. Ask real questions. Give real answers. Build real connections.

## The Power of Video: More Human, More Visible

Video isn’t just a trend, it’s one of the most effective ways to connect.

[LinkedIn videos](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuablee_aiinnovation-workplacetransformation-generativeai-activity-7287536708278005760-BJI1?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) are up [36% year-over-year](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/linkedin-shares-more-tips-maximizing-video-content-performance-infographic/732893/), and with 75% of U.S. adults spending up to two hours daily watching short-form video, it’s clear: Video is king. It’s not about the views; it’s about the value.

What’s the lesson here? Numbers don’t mean much if the content doesn’t connect. Your job is to spark dialogue, not just rack up views.

Here’s how to nail short unproduced video:

🔵 Start Strong: Hook your audience in the first 10 seconds.

🔵 Keep It Real: Ditch the scripts and share something honest.

🔵 Make It Accessible: Use captions, 80% of people are more likely to finish videos with subtitles.

## Will You Step Up?

If you’re treating LinkedIn like a boring resume site, you’re wasting its potential. This platform isn’t just about jobs, [it’s about influence](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/coca-cola-snoop-dogg-you-insights-building-powerful-personal-lee-ngh1c/?trackingId=Z9hoBGqmTtqVmRksUnU7Lw%3D%3D), impact, and owning your space as a leader.

So, here’s your challenge:

➡️ Optimize Your Profile: Make sure it tells the story of who you are AND what you do.

➡️ Engage With Trending News: Stop lurking. Start contributing. Pick one trending topic this week and share your take on it.

➡️ Create Videos: Show up authentically. Use video to connect, inspire, and lead.

The digital world is loud, messy, and fast-paced, but LinkedIn is the steady platform where leaders are built. The only question is: Are you showing up, or are you sitting it out? Are you building your legacy, or are you invisible?

Let’s be real: LinkedIn isn’t just for job hunting or humblebragging anymore. It’s your stage, and the audience? Your ideal connections just waiting to hit “follow.”

The [StandOut Authority Experience On-Demand](https://standoutauthority.com/standout-authority-experience-on-demand/?vgo_ee=tuFAkWoZRDmKuE9%2B3Fy92o%2FxYZlyS7J2UFF8k4dThnb2eEwyEjXZGQzbnA%3D%3D%3AIs%2BMZ%2BFtQu%2FETO3tNSJKWDMphAXoGEcP)****is here to help you stop lurking, start leading, and turn those casual scrolls into real opportunities.

Because it's not just about “likes”—it’s about building trust, sharing value, and turning connections into your biggest cheerleaders.

Ready to step into your LinkedIn presence with purpose?

**Start here**👉 [StandOut Authority Experience On-Demand](https://standoutauthority.com/standout-authority-experience-on-demand/?vgo_ee=tuFAkWoZRDmKuE9%2B3Fy92o%2FxYZlyS7J2UFF8k4dThnb2eEwyEjXZGQzbnA%3D%3D%3AIs%2BMZ%2BFtQu%2FETO3tNSJKWDMphAXoGEcP)

2025-vision-leaders-transforming-connect.excerpt: Will You Lead the Future or Watch It Pass You By? The future isn’t coming, it’s already here. The leaders who will thrive in 2025 aren’t sitting back, hoping to “ride it out.” They’re leani
2025-vision-leaders-transforming-connect.body:
## Will You Lead the Future or Watch It Pass You By?

The future isn’t coming, it’s already here. The leaders who will thrive in 2025 aren’t sitting back, hoping to “ride it out.” They’re leaning in, embracing tools like AI and video, not to replace what makes them human, but to amplify it. But thriving in 2025 isn’t just about shiny tools or chasing trends, it’s about showing up with authenticity.

It’s about mastering 3 key strategies that will help you lead with impact while building connection and trust:

🔵 Using AI as your co-pilot

🔵 Making video your connection superpower

🔵 Building trust through thought leadership

Here’s how you can turn these strategies into action.

## 1. AI: The Mirror That Amplifies Your Strengths

Some see AI as a job stealer, others as a magic wand. I see it differently: **AI is a mirror. **

It reflects the intentions of those who use it. If you lean on AI to cut corners, it will expose the cracks in your foundation. But if you embrace it as a tool to amplify your strengths, your creativity, leadership, and ability to connect, it will help you soar.

Here’s what I mean. AI can write a LinkedIn post in 30 seconds, but only YOU can decide if that post tells the story of who you are. It can analyze trends faster than you can say "2025," but only YOU can choose what truly matters to your audience.

> **AI isn’t here to replace you. It’s here to remind you what makes you irreplaceable.**

For me, tools like [CopyAndContent.AI](http://CopyAndContent.AI) and Jasper AI have been my co-pilot. They help me brainstorm, shape ideas, and create content, but they don’t replace my voice. And that’s the key: AI isn’t here to _do_ your job. It’s here to give you back time so you can lead with impact.

Real talk: my son Jayden calls AI my “work babysitter.” And honestly? He’s not wrong. By taking on repetitive tasks, AI gives me the bandwidth to show up more fully for my family, my team, and my clients.

**The takeaway for 2025:** AI will never replace the human spark. Use it to save time but let your authenticity shine through. You are the connection!

## 2. Video: The Most Human Way to Lead Digitally

Video isn’t just “the next big thing.” It’s the thing.

LinkedIn videos are up 36% year-over-year, and with [75%](https://topics-na1.emarketer.com/topic/digital-video)of U.S. adults spending up to two hours a day watching short-form video, ignoring video isn’t an option, it’s a missed opportunity. But here’s what I’ve learned from my own content: it’s not about the views. It’s about the value.

Let me give you a real-world example. I posted a video on LinkedIn about [Red Dye #3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuablee_reddyeban-awareness-healthmatters-activity-7285672038139150337-_cNd?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop), something totally unrelated to business, and it hit nearly 5K views. The kicker? It sparked an authentic conversation in the comments that I never expected.

Now, let’s flip the script. I [posted a video breaking down the economy](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuablee_opportunity-jobmarket-humantohuman-activity-7283989249803132930-unOw?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) and jobs report, something highly relevant to my audience. It hit 210K impressions with over 14K views, but the engagement? Way lower than I thought it’d be.

Here’s the lesson: the real magic happens when your video connects, not just when it performs. High numbers might catch your attention, but it’s the moments that spark conversations and build relationships that actually matter.

**How to Nail Video in 2025:**

🔵 Lead with a hook, those first 10 seconds make or break your video.

🔵 Ditch the script, people want YOU, not perfection.

🔵 Use captions, [80%](https://www.nexttv.com/news/mobile-videos-often-watched-without-audio-study-finds) of viewers are more likely to finish a video with subtitles.

Your challenge for 2025? **Stop overthinking video.** Use it to show your human side. Whether you’re talking about business, family, or something as random as Red Dye #3, let people see the real YOU. That’s how you build connection, trust, and leadership that lasts.

## 3. Thought Leadership: The Ultimate Trust Builder

Let’s get one thing straight: people don’t follow perfect leaders. They follow _real_ ones.

Thought leadership isn’t about having all the answers, it’s about sharing the journey. It’s about showing up with stories, insights, and perspectives that inspire trust. And trust? That’s the currency of leadership.

Case in point: a [Dopamine Dose edition](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/beyond-numbers-game-cultivating-high-value-connections-joshua-b-lee-8nmwc/?trackingId=L07j9nZUTgaV2Dc5Xi3qQw%3D%3D) about connection on LinkedIn sparked one of the most meaningful conversations I’ve had online. It wasn’t polished or strategic, it was honest. And that resonated.

**How to lead with thought leadership in 2025:**

🔵 Share lessons from failure, it’s where the best insights come from.

🔵 Ask questions that spark meaningful conversations.

🔵 Engage authentically, respond to comments, don’t just broadcast.

The [2024 Edelman-LinkedIn B2B Thought Leadership Impact Report](https://www.edelman.com/expertise/Business-Marketing/2024-b2b-thought-leadership-report) found that 73% of decision-makers trust thought leadership over ads. Why? Because it’s real. It’s relatable. And it shows you’re more than just a pitch, you’re a person.

**The 2025 mindset:** Stop trying to be perfect. Start being present.

## The Leadership Challenge for 2025

Here’s the reality: technology will keep evolving, but the leaders who thrive will be the ones who stay human.Source Credit Imgflip

So, here’s your challenge:

🔵 Use AI to create space for what matters most.

🔵 Use video to connect authentically and spark real conversations.

🔵 Lead with thought leadership to build trust and inspire action.

2025 isn’t about keeping up with trends, it’s about amplifying what makes you unforgettable. So, what’s your move? Drop your thoughts in the comments. Let’s make 2025 the year we lead with heart, authenticity, and connection.

📢 **ICYMI:** Did you catch my LinkedIn LIVE with [Rachel B. Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/therachelblee?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAATthuAB-Gy4FMm8KnvDftaFczqyPAUOIsI) ?

AI, social media, leadership, and marketing are shifting everything we thought we knew, and if you’re not adapting, you’re falling behind.

Rachel had me on her LinkedIn LIVE, and we got straight to the point: no fluff, no gimmicks, just real strategies for leaders who are ready to step up and lead in this new landscape.

**Here’s what we dove into:**

🔵How to use AI as a tool _without losing your humanity_

🔵Why genuine relationships will always outperform flashy campaigns (trust is the currency of leadership)

🔵Meta’s bold move: The ripple effects of free speech and content regulation for brands, businesses, and leaders like you

📢 This isn’t just a conversation; it’s a call to action. [Watch the replay](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/therachelblee_linkedinlive-marketing-ai-activity-7283513033132228610-l8x0?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)and let’s make 2025 a year of real leadership and meaningful impact.
