boost-b2b-marketing-linkedin-social-sell.body:
How well do you know LinkedIn? Most B2B marketers are familiar with its basic features, but few know it well enough to leverage the network for lead generation. Social selling has been around for a while, mastering the art of creating social relationships to drive business has become a top priority for anyone in B2B marketing.

## What’s Social Selling, Anyway?

Despite the long work hours, substantial investment in marketing, and efforts to connect with influencers, many businesses still don’t have enough clients.

Why? Well, it’s because they are unaware of how to generate leads via social, particularly on LinkedIn. Before drilling down into how social selling works, here is a definition of the concept, for those who are less familiar with it.

## How LinkedIn Can Help You Find Prospects

First, disregard anyone who tells you that selling on LinkedIn is only for spammers. There’s no denying that a fair share of spam exists on the network. All of us have encountered promotional InMails, fake connection requests, and group posts with zero relation to the discussion at hand.

However, don’t let this discourage you! LinkedIn is an excellent place for relationship building. Marketers who use authentic and helpful strategies will be recognized (and hopefully rewarded) for their efforts. Social selling is all about engagement, and if a prospect is willing to engage with you on social, you never know if it will result in a one-time purchase, or even a life-long corporate client.

In B2B marketing, social media is about so much more than counting likes, shares, and retweets. More specifically, social selling is about getting results, including converting prospects into clients, generating increased brand awareness, and positioning your brands an industry thought leader.

## Looking for Leads? Use LinkedIn’s Sales Navigator

Engaging on social media is all about making prospects feel like you’ve taken the time to read about them, and familiarize yourself with their interests, company background, and pain points. Even taking a few minutes to read through a user’s LinkedIn timeline or Twitter feed can reveal a lot, and give you a great starting point for discussion.

Before you begin your research, the first step is to find actual prospects to connect with, and LinkedIn’s Sales Navigator is the ultimate weapon for this. You can look up prospects by name, company, title, geographic location and more.

**Secret LinkedIn Research Tip #1: Use Boolean Search Operators**

To really find the perfect prospect, a secret tip is to incorporate [Boolean search operators](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/75814/using-boolean-search-on-linkedin?lang=en), primarily AND, OR, AND NOT. LinkedIn’s Boolean searches look at a user’s entire profile, including the summary and headline, and deliver incredibly refined results for finding B2B marketing prospects.

For instance, if you’re searching for decision-makers in sales or in marketing, use OR: “(marketing OR sales)”, which would bring back results for anyone with a marketing or sales background. However, if you combine this with “(manager OR director OR VP)”, you’ll find a combination of people at these different levels.

When you’re unsure of someone’s exact title or company name, or if you’d like to exclude a certain person or industry from your search, this can come in quit handy. Here’s a very helpful [tip sheet from LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/76015/using-search-operators-on-linkedin?lang=en)that details exactly how to use these operators.

**Secret LinkedIn Research Tip #2: Save Your Searches**

Did you know that LinkedIn searches can be saved? With [Sales Navigator LinkedIn lets you save searches](https://www.linkedin.com/help/sales-navigator/answer/50237/saving-a-search-in-sales-navigator?lang=en) and set up alerts based on the parameters you set.

Once you save a search, LinkedIn will email you with new prospects who meet your search criteria.

Once you start receiving a list of prospects, reach out on LinkedIn by:

- Inviting them to connect (tip: personalize the message!)

- Asking a mutual connection via the [mobile app](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/74110)

- Joining a Discussion Group they’re a member of

- Sending them a direct message (if you’re both part of the same Group)

- Sending them an InMail (Premium account only)

- Commenting on one of their LinkedIn Publishing posts

**Before Contacting a Prospect, Make Sure…**

A) Your LinkedIn Profile Is Complete

All of the fields in your [LinkedIn profile](http://topdogsocialmedia.com/linkedin-marketing-infographic/) should be complete (and up-to-date), you have a professional-looking head shot, you’ve grown your network of connections. Bonus tip: it’s great to have at least a few LinkedIn Endorsements and Recommendations.

Also, is your contact info filled in? In your profile, click on Contact Info in the right-hand corner of your profile photo box, and fill out your email, website, blog, Twitter handle, and any other details.

B) You’ve Already Researched the Prospect

Before you reach out, do your research first. LinkedIn and Twitter offer a wealth of insight into the person’s interests, social media activity, and expertise. Even doing a simple Google search on the prospect’s name, and reading through his or her company’s website, can be helpful.

For example, read through the person’s entire LinkedIn profile. Then, to see recent activity, click on the prospect’s profile, click on the drop-down under the “Send a Message” button, and select View Recent activity. Check how active your prospects are on the network, read any publishing posts they’ve written and any status updates they’ve shared.

In addition, use the LinkedIn Contact Details section to see if a Twitter handle is listed, and read through their most recent tweets to learn more. Once you’ve done your homework, it will be much easier to craft a personalized, relevant message which more likely to receive attention – and a reply.

## Time to Engage with Your LinkedIn Prospects

As any B2B marketing expert knows, LinkedIn isn’t just for generating new leads, it’s also an excellent tool for engaging with them. The platform offers a few different options, both public (status updates, Discussion Groups) and private (Inmails, direct messages) in nature.

**Public Engagement on LinkedIn: Status Updates**

Some people feel that no one reads the LinkedIn News Feed, but it turns out, they actually do. I recommend posting to your news feed 1-2 times a day to generate engagement.

Once you start posting regularly, people will begin to like, share, and comment on your content. Remember that every comment left on a post is chance to engage. Click on the prospect’s profile, determine whether or not he or she is a relevant, and reach out.

Below are 3 quick tips you can use to create great LinkedIn status updates:

- Tag people and companies in personal posts using “@”

- Upload files to your posts (JPEGs, PDFs, Word documents)

- Customize the image in your link attachment preview

**Public Engagement on LinkedIn: Publishing Platform**

If you have more time to invest, start writing long-form posts like this one using LinkedIn’s Publishing platform, to express your interests and expertise. Once only open to elite influencers, the platform is now available to all users. Any post published will be shared with your connections and followers, will be searchable on and off LinkedIn, and may even be published as content in Pulse.

In terms of B2B marketing, posts are an excellent way to repurpose content, showcase your knowledge, and grow your followers and visibility. It can also help cement your thought leadership, which is key to building the trust and credibility you need for social selling.

The easiest way to ensure success is creating an editorial calendar for posts, developing an excellent distribution strategy, and reading up on how to optimize your posts.

What makes a great LinkedIn publishing post?

- Catchy title (optimal length: up to 50 characters)

- Attractive visuals (especially the top featured image)

- Sub-headers throughout the content for easy reading

- Intelligent use of keywords to make the content “searchable”

- Providing valuable insights – not a promotional pitch

- Including a call-to-action at the end of the post

If you publish or read a LinkedIn post that’s especially relevant for a prospect, you can share the link as a status update, and tag that person. In this respect, take notes for each LinkedIn contact under the Relationship tab. Cite which content you’ve shared with them, and remember schedule follow-up reminders. This will ensure that your content stays top-of-mind with the prospect, making it easier to eventually push them down the funnel.

**Private Engagement on LinkedIn: Direct Messages**

If you prefer to adopt a more personal, 1:1 approach, LinkedIn offers a few options for private engagement, primarily InMail and direct messages. If you only remember one thing after reading is, it should be to do your research before reaching out, especially if it’s through a private message.

Regardless of whether you do a Google search, review recent activity on LinkedIn or Twitter, or read up about a company website, when corresponding with a prospect, mention something you’ve come across in your research to show that you’ve done your homework.

When writing a personal message, follow the below advice:

- Introduce yourself, and quickly get to the point of why you’re writing

- Reference the research you’ve done by personalizing the message

- Avoid being promotional, and don’t beg or plead

- Ask for advice, or mention a certain pain point

**Private Engagement on LinkedIn: InMails**

On LinkedIn, with a free account, you can only send messages to anyone who is a connection in your network. InMails are paid-for messages that you use when someone is outside of your network (3rd level or beyond), not a friend of a friend, and with whom you have no shared groups.

If you have a free account, you’ll need to upgrade to LinkedIn Premium to send an InMail to someone outside of your network. With Premium, you receive a certain number of InMail credits depending on your subscription.

In the past, you would get your InMail “back” if your message didn’t receive a response within a certain number of days. However, this policy was reversed, and users will only get back InMails if a reply is received.

Don't want to pay for InMails? there's a way to reach prospects outside of your network, [for free](https://help.linkedin.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/192/~/communicating-with-a-fellow-group-member). Scroll down to the bottom of the prospect’s profile, look at which Groups he or she is a member of, and join the most relevant one. Then, in the Group itself, click on the Members hyperlink in the top, search for the name of the prospect, and underneath it, click on “Send Message”.

## Bonus LinkedIn Tip: Data Export Tool

One final secret on LinkedIn to boost your B2B marketing, that lets you export all of your valuable data. Under your profile photo in the top right corner, click on “Manage” to the right of Privacy & Settings. Then, click on the Account tab, and under the Helpful Links category, click on “Request an archive of your data.”

On you receive the archive, the prospecting opportunities are endless! The data includes everything from ad interactions, endorsements, and previous successful search queries. Review the information, and start thinking of new strategies for reaching your B2B marketing prospects more successfully!

what-social-selling-through-linkedin-how.body:
If you were to enter any sales office in the country and ask what the latest buzzword is at meetings and water cooler talk, it will likely be "social selling." Social selling has become the new hot topic nobody can stop talking about, mainly because of the influential culture social media has introduced to modern society.

Social selling is popular among sales professionals because of its vast outreach potential. In fact, We Are Social stated that there are more than [3 billion active social media accounts at the start of 2017](https://wearesocial.com/blog/2017/08/three-billion-people-now-use-social-media). What salesperson wouldn't want to tap into that goldmine? However, what is social selling, exactly, and how can real estate agents use it to increase their sales goals? LinkedIn has tapped into that unanswered inquiry and created a program that measures an individual's social selling ability: [the Social Selling Index.](https://business.linkedin.com/sales-solutions/social-selling/the-social-selling-index-ssi)

**What Is Social Selling on LinkedIn?**

LinkedIn is the most popular professional social media platform in America. According to LinkedIn, "social selling is about leveraging your professional social network to find the right prospects, build trusted relationships, and ultimately, achieve your sales goals." To help you understand your social selling skills, LinkedIn measures the following four main categories:

**1. Establishment of Your Professional Brand:**

- Complete your profile with the customer in mind. Share with others what you can bring to the table and why you would be the right fit for the professional needs in your niche market.

- Add rich Content Highlight you as a thought leader. Include examples of your work on your profile in rich media to share with prospects and customers in an interactive way.

- Increase visibility by posting and interacting with content. Make it your goal to share high quality information that is helpful and contextually appropriate for followers.

- Generate endorsements for customers and colleagues. (Expert tip~endorsing connections on LinkedIn often prompts them to return the favor)

- List your skills as a simple, efficient way to show your prospects how you can help them

**2. Focus on the Right Prospects:**

- Don't spin your wheels reaching out to just anybody. Hone in on the right tools and search methods to discover viable prospects.

- Leverage warm introductions to expand your network

- Look for commonalities to establish a relationship

- Take advantage of who’s viewed your profile. Your activity drives views of your profile. Review often and engage with relevant viewers.

**3. Engagement With Insights:**

- Keep informed of current news and trends in your industry and share them.

- Become the expert in your field. Post relevant content that can help you become the trusted source of insights

- Identify information for prospects that shows you care about their success and tag them when you share

- Stay in the know with timely content by leveraging industry data and news on LinkedIn to stay up to date.

- Leave thoughtful, constructive comments on content your prospects share or join LinkedIn Groups

- Always customize messages using relevant information you have learned about the person on LinkedIn

**4. Building of Trusted Relationships:**

- Connect with other users and start building on the foundation of trust that's necessary for procuring successful relationships.

- A larger network gives you greater leverage in finding new prospects and getting in the door with clients

- Focus on decisions makers (Build multiple connections with decisions makers, don’t rely on just one)

- After connecting, develop the relationship just as you would have before LinkedIn existed, reaching out periodically at appropriate times and adding value

- Help prospects by sharing their updates and post they’ve published

**How Is the Social Selling Index Score Obtained?**

LinkedIn rates a user's social selling skills with a score from zero to 100. The score is based on the depth and quality of activity based on each of the four main categories. According to the LinkedIn Help Center, measurements are taken on the following:

- How complete your profile is, any long-form posts you've written, and the followers that have resulted from it

- The amount of connections you have and the rate of acceptance with those connections

- Your social animation, including comments, messages, and groups joined

- Your profile views, people searches, and days active

**Why Is the Social Selling Index Score Important?**

LinkedIn proves that the higher the score, the more successful a person is at reaching his or her sales goals. The site claims that highly active LinkedIn users gain 45 percent more sales opportunities, are 51 percent are more likely to hit their quota, and are 80 percent more productive. Everyone Social offers similar findings, explaining that Microsoft saw an increase of 4.3 more opportunities with every 10 points raised on the index. The score is not a miracle cure for increased sales, but it does show a strong correlation between specific networking activity and an increase in sales opportunities.

LinkedIn's Social Selling Index has created an impressive calculation system to measure your social selling capabilities. When used actively and correctly, the numbers should yield positive results. What this index fails to do, however, is to measure the end results for you.

After all is said and done, YOU will need to be accountable for investing in the right search tools, training yourself on the methods, and keeping track of how your level of activity drives your bottom line.

Thank you for taking time out of your day to read my recent article.

linkedin-ads-why-how-integrate-your-soci.body:
Wondering how to best integrate LinkedIn, the world’s largest professional network, into your social strategy? LinkedIn advertising could be just the ticket, especially if you are a marketer.

The great advantage of LinkedIn is that it is a uniquely focused social network—it’s all business, all the time. This makes it the ideal network for B2B organizations in particular. And with LinkedIn ads, businesses can choose from a range of ads to target and reach the right people when they’re in a business-y frame of mind.

Find out how LinkedIn went from buttoned-up digital resume platform to content marketing rockstar, growing to 500 million users in the process. And learn why and how you can use LinkedIn ads to join the party… sorry, business meeting. (Don’t forget the doughnuts.)

## Why use LinkedIn ads?

It hasn’t been easy for LinkedIn to find its place in the world. In fact, for a long time it was hard to get the point of the network. You signed up, tried to find a semi-professional looking photo, and added your coworkers. Then what?

Today, LinkedIn is a different, much more interesting and useful place for users—and marketers, especially with the help of LinkedIn ads, the ins and outs of which we’ll get to shortly.

What changed?

LinkedIn introduced some pretty significant feature and usability upgrades to help build its community to the point where [40 percent](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/2016-linkedin-stats-you-should-know-updated-katy-elle-blake?published=t) of users visit the site every day. These include:

- Better mobile apps.

- Slicker desktop version.

- Richer content features.

- Better spam management.

- Video.

The richer user experience now makes LinkedIn somewhere people want to hang out. According to LinkedIn’s [stats](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/audience), those people include 61 million influencers, 40 million decision-makers, and 10 million opinion leaders—in other words “the world’s professionals.” In an [AdWeek article](http://www.adweek.com/digital/once-a-running-joke-linkedin-is-suddenly-a-hot-social-network-heres-what-changed/) charting LinkedIn’s growth, Jessie Liu, senior analyst at Forrester Research, said: “More than most social networks, LinkedIn has very robust and deep user data. It’s collecting your location, educational history, professional history and interests. That makes it far more valuable than, say, Twitter.”

LinkedIn advertising lets marketers leverage this gold mine of data, offering several hard-to-ignore benefits:

- [Advanced targeting features](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/ad-targeting), including job title, function, and industry.

- A broad range of ad options, including [self-serve ads](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/ads) and [partner solutions](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/marketing-partners).

- Flexible [budget controls](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/ads/pricing).

- Lead generation tools to increase conversion.

- [Tracking and analytics tools](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/conversion-tracking) to measure performance.

- Multiple language options.

LinkedIn ads even offer guaranteed impressions. Before you pay a dime, you can create your LinkedIn ad and see exactly how big of an audience you are going to reach.

But does it work? Do people use LinkedIn to discover and engage with content? According to LinkedIn’s own data, [content gets 15 times the interaction of job postings](https://business.linkedin.com/content/dam/me/business/en-us/marketing-solutions/products/pdfs/LISponsoredContentDatasheet5-2-16.pdf).

 The benefits of LinkedIn and LinkedIn ads to marketers are clear. Let’s get into the nitty-gritty of how to advertise on LinkedIn, starting with my guide to LinkedIn ad formats.

## Types of LinkedIn ads

Whether you want to target executives, influencers, or job seekers, there are various ways to advertise on LinkedIn through different ad types, including self-serve, partner programs, and other options. Each type of LinkedIn ad comes with its own benefits and best practices.

### LinkedIn self-serve ads

You can create and publish your own ads through LinkedIn’s [Campaign Manager](https://www.linkedin.com/uas/login?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fad%2Faccounts). Campaign Manager allows you to schedule campaigns in advance, target the right audience, and see the industries, job functions, and seniority level of users who click your ads. If you have the time and resources to do that, this could be the easiest option for you. It’s also a great way to dip your toe into LinkedIn advertising.

There are currently three ad options to choose from, with video ads said by LinkedIn to be rolled out in 2018:

### Sponsored Content

[Sponsored Content](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/native-advertising) lets you share posts to your Company Page with a targeted audience on LinkedIn. It helps you amplify company news, promotions, relevant industry articles, SlideShare presentations, and Vimeo and YouTube videos.

The ads appear in the homepage feed (on desktop, mobile, and tablet) and on the right side of the desktop homepage. For example, if you have a one-day-only sale or a video of a recent company charity event, a sponsored update is the best way to get that content out to a wider audience.

### Why use Sponsored Content?

- Extend the reach of your content.

- Attract more Company Page followers.

- Capture eyeballs and clicks on desktop, tablet, and mobile.

- Integrate LinkedIn’s lead generation [forms](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/native-advertising/lead-gen-ads).

View LinkedIn’s advertising [specs and guidelines](https://www.linkedin.com/help/lms/topics/8154/8155/68894) for Sponsored Content.

### Text Ads

[Text Ads](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/ppc-advertising) let you advertise on LinkedIn to drive traffic to your LinkedIn Company Page or your website. This is a quick and easy desktop-only option that lets you feature a compelling headline, a description, and an eye-catching image in a variety of ad formats. Your ads may appear under “Ads You May Be Interested In” and as text link advertisements found at the top of the page. If you want to grab the attention of a busy professional browsing LinkedIn, including promoting a job opening, Text Ads are a good way to go.

### Why use Text Ads?

- Fast and easy to get started.

- Set your own budget.

- Choose your audience with laser sharp B2B filters.

- Track conversions.

View LinkedIn’s advertising [specs and guidelines](https://www.linkedin.com/help/lms/topics/8154/8155/71241) for Text Ads.

### Sponsored InMail

[Sponsored InMail](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/sponsored-inmail) enables you to send personalized messages to targeted LinkedIn users through LinkedIn’s email client, LinkedIn Messenger. Recipients only receive Sponsored InMails when they are active on LinkedIn to help them get noticed. It’s an effective option if you want to go for a more personalized approach to drive conversion rates.

### Why use Sponsored InMail?

- Send personalized invites to webinars and other events.

- Target promotions to the right audience.

- Promote content, such as downloadable ebooks and white papers.

View LinkedIn’s advertising [specs and guidelines](https://www.linkedin.com/help/lms/topics/8154/8155/68895) for Sponsored InMail.

### LinkedIn Display Ads

[Display Ads](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/display-advertising) is LinkedIn’s programmatic advertising solution. This means you can purchase ads through your preferred advertising platform or a private or public auction.

Display ads allow for a greater variety of media, including text, audio, video, and images, which makes them more eye-catching and interactive.

This is a good option to help you get your business in front of your desired audience early in the buying cycle and increase awareness on a large scale.

### Why use Display Ads?

- Reach more professionals, thought leaders, decision-makers, and influencers.

- Create more engaging and eye-catching ads.

- Get ad placement on high-traffic LinkedIn pages.

View LinkedIn’s advertising [specs and guidelines](https://www.linkedin.com/help/lms/topics/8154/8155/68892) for Display Ads.

### LinkedIn Dynamic Ads

[Dynamic Ads](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/dynamic-ads) are highly customizable personalized ads. They are dynamically generated according to your audience’s activity. For example, if LinkedIn knows someone is searching for a job in your industry, you can target them at the right time with the right messages. You can write your own ad copy, choose your call to action, and use dynamically generated images from LinkedIn member profiles.

This kind of advertising is especially useful for building relationships and delivering personalized messages to the most influential members of your audience. It’s a great way to really make people sit up and take notice.

### Why use Dynamic Ads?

- Deliver compelling, personalized messages to increase response.

- Choose from a range of targeting criteria.

- Generate specific actions through customized calls to action.

- Grow your Company Page’s followers.

View LinkedIn’s advertising [specs and guidelines](https://www.linkedin.com/help/lms/topics/8154/8155/68893) for Dynamic Ads.

##

## How to advertise on LinkedIn: a step-by-step guide

Before you can do anything, you need a Company Page to run Sponsored Content ads, and it’s a good thing to set up in any case.

 **How to advertise on LinkedIn with self-serve ads**

Getting started with self-serve LinkedIn ads is easy. Follow these six steps, which are outlined in more detail [here](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/how-to-advertise-on-linkedin).

### Step 1: Set up a Campaign Manager account

This really does just take a couple of minutes. You can create multiple accounts.

### Step 2: Choose your ad type

Select the type of ad you want to create. You can create an entire campaign using all three formats for maximum impact and reach.

Each of the three options will require you to create a campaign name and choose your target audience language. With Sponsored Content ads you also need to select a call-to-action option:

**Step 3: Create your ad**

Campaign Manager walks you through the process of creating the various different ads, providing ad specs and tips along the way. For example, here are the options for creating a Text Ad:

### Step 4: Target your ad

Next you get a range of options for targeting your ad to the right people, including location, company names, school names, job functions, skills, and other filters. You can save your choices as a template to speed things up when creating other campaigns.

### Step 5: Choose your budget and schedule

You can choose from cost per click (CPC) or cost per impression (CPM), or cost per send for Sponsored InMail ads (which means you only pay when your message is delivered). For CPC and CPM, you can set a daily spend limit and a bid price, which is the most you want to pay per click or impression. You can also choose a start and finish date for your campaign.

At this stage you can also add [conversion tracking](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/67513) (Sponsored Content and Text Ads only). It lets you track specific actions so you can better measure, and then improve, ROI. These include sign-ups, installs, downloads, and purchases.

### Step 6: Measure and refine your LinkedIn ads

LinkedIn ads Campaign Manger gives you access to a range of metrics to help you measure and optimize your campaigns. These include impressions, clicks, and spend. LinkedIn also lets you measure “social actions,” which capture how LinkedIn members interact with your content.

### How to advertise on LinkedIn with other types of ads

To advertise on LinkedIn using the other other options, follow the links from these pages to get started:

- [Get started with LinkedIn Display Ads](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/display-advertising).

- [Get started with LinkedIn Dynamic Ads](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/dynamic-ads).

## Self-serve LinkedIn Ad tips and best practices

Succeeding with each of the self-serve ad types involves focusing on a few key areas in particular.

### Sponsored Content quick tips

- Use an eye-catching image.

- Add URL tracking codes to measure site visits or conversions.

- Keep the accompanying copy to under 150 characters.

- Focus on the audience with the highest engagement rate.

### Text Ad quick tips

- Make use of the image option to attract eyeballs.

- Include a strong, specific call to action.

- Write a compelling headline.

- Talk directly to your audience and use active language.

### Sponsored InMail quick tips

- Address the recipient by name.

- Keep it concise (under 1,000 characters).

- Include a clear call to action.

- Write a compelling subject line that shows the value of your offering.

 **General LinkedIn ad tips and best practices**

Here are some more general LinkedIn ad tips and best practices.

### Write strong, compelling copy

Strong copy demands the attention of the reader. The best way to do this is to offer interesting insights while keeping your message simple. Demonstrate your understanding of the industry, but keep jargon to a minimum or you’ll generate “zzzzz”s instead of clicks.

 **Include relevant images**

Relevant images are an essential part of social media content marketing. But finding a great image to catch the eye of your prospect can be tough, especially if your budget is tight.

Hootsuite did a roundup of [20 free photo sites for stock social media images](https://blog.hootsuite.com/20-free-stock-photo-sites-social-media-images/) and its a great place to start.

### Target by group

Targeting by group is a great way to reach people who may be interested in your product or service. To make sure you target the right groups, you’ll need to dig around a little before you get started. It’s helpful if you’ve already taken some time to build audience personas. Discover which groups your ideal buyers belong to and then compile a shortlist of professional or trade associations you want to target.

According to a [webcast](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/blog/linkedin-sponsored-updates/2016/ask-the-experts--the-insiders-guide-to-targeting) with LinkedIn content campaign strategist Pavels Kilivniks and team lead Katerina Ram, breaking up your B2B target audience by demographic can be a helpful tool for targeting. Here are three good ones to consider:

- **Job title and function** are key professional attributes of your audience. LinkedIn ads allow you to search and create audiences composed of specific criteria. So if you want to sell specialized medical equipment to radio brain surgeons in Kalamazoo, Michigan, LinkedIn will help you find them.

- **Industry and company size** tell you who your next buyer could be. Do you want to sell to a large company or a small business? Are you targeting all the software engineers in Silicon Valley or dairy lobbyists in your home state? Refine your aim with a precise target.

- **Seniority** is a great way to target influencers with your LinkedIn ads. LinkedIn pulls data from member profiles even if they don’t have the word “senior” in their title.

- For example, if a person has been with a company for more than two years, that person will be mapped as an individual contributor and will appear as “senior” in the [Campaign Manager tool](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/blog/linkedin-news/2016/we_re-making-linkedin-advertising-easier-than-ever-with-these-ne). The algorithm is able to determine if a particular member is entry-level or not because it accounts for their entire career path.

### Test, test, and test again

Test a different version of each LinkedIn ad to see which one brings in the most business. With the text ad option, you can you can create up to 15 variations of one ad. Change the image, headline, text, and destination to see who bites and when.

### Budget and bid wisely

Budgeting and bidding effectively is crucial. You can choose to set your LinkedIn advertising bid and campaign budget by [cost per click (CPC)](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/1392) or [cost per thousand impressions (CPM)](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/1392). If you choose to go the CPC route you can specify the maximum amount you’re willing to pay for each click. This is the best option if your campaign is direct response. If you decide to go with CPM, you pay up to your maximum bid each time your ad is shown 1,000 times on LinkedIn, no matter how many clicks you receive. This is the method LinkedIn suggests if your advertising strategy is creating brand awareness.

### Measure to improve ROI

Measuring your LinkedIn ads’ performance helps you maximize your social media ROI. You can use the LinkedIn ads Campaign Manager to track performance by monitoring impressions, clicks, costs, and other metrics. With each new campaign you’ll learn what’s working and what’s not.

The cost of LinkedIn ads tends to run a little higher than other social media platforms so you will want to pay close attention to your analytics.

That’s our guide to LinkedIn ads—a great way for social marketers to reach professionals. Now go update your profile pic. That one of you on vacation with the straw from your Pina Colada showing just won’t cut it anymore.

Thank you for taking time out of your day to learn how to optimize your LinkedIn Advertising

~ Joshua B Lee

social-selling-whats-behind-hype-joshua-.title: Social Selling - What's Behind The Hype?
social-selling-whats-behind-hype-joshua-.excerpt: Despite all the hype surrounding social selling, only 8% of companies identified social selling as a "top sales priority." (Cue the sound of crickets chirping.) Social selling has become a…
social-selling-whats-behind-hype-joshua-.body:
Despite all the hype surrounding social selling, only 8% of companies identified social selling as a "top sales priority." (Cue the sound of crickets chirping.) Social selling has become a cottage industry. There is no shortage of "LinkedIn experts" offering to help optimize your social selling efforts, but how many people are actually closing deals as a result of social selling? Here's my opinion on what's behind the social selling hype and why so many are failing at it.

### What social selling isn't

Far too many social sellers have simply transferred annoying sales practices from one medium to another. When today’s buyer wants information about a product or service, they are looking for material that is useful, relevant and, most of all, not overly “salesy”. Having learned that cold calling is producing diminishing returns, these "social sellers" are now using a similar approach on LinkedIn. We've all seen it - you receive a request to connect on LinkedIn. You accept. Faster than the beat of a hummingbird's wings, you receive a LinkedIn message from your new connection. It's a generic sales pitch with absolutely no context to your unique situation. I'm fairly inclusive about accepting connection requests, but this "social selling" tactic is making me rethink that.

I have had many lead generation "experts" use this approach with me. A minimal amount of research ( taking two seconds to review my profile) would show that I help other businesses generate conversions, not just traffic. And even 30 seconds of research would allow these "social sellers" to qualify me out of their sales process, saving us both time. What they've done is transfer annoying sales practices from the telephone to LinkedIn. The prevalence of these practices has a lot to do with the fact that business leaders are just starting to attach importance to social selling.

### What social selling should be

In my opinion, social selling is more of a tool than a sales channel. I'm not saying that you shouldn't use social media to generate sales leads, but you need to be respectful and helpful with your social sales outreaches and offer value first. Here are few tips for your outbound social selling.

1.    **ALWAYS use context in your outbound social selling**. Do research on the person you're approaching and their company and explain how your solution could potentially help them.

2.    **Get to the point!** People are busy and don't have time to read your 5,000 word capabilities statement. If someone approaches me and briefly shows me that they have taken the time to research me and my company, I try to at least give them the courtesy of a response. Unfortunately, most people that approach me don't do that.

3.    **Be respectful.** Cyber stalking is scary and is not going to close deals for you.

Your social selling is significantly more effective when the person you're approaching has some awareness of you and your company when you're reaching out.

### How to use social selling as a tool

Social media is best used as a tool to support your integrated sales and marketing efforts. The concept behind social media is that it is a two-way conversation in which participants can choose subjects and people to interact with. If you respect those principles and earn trust, selling will be a natural progression of the communications process. Here are some suggestions on how you can gain trust and build relationships to help you sell.

1.    **Use social media to promote your content**. If you're not producing **content that is helpful to your customers and prospects**, you should be. Promote your content on your company's social media accounts first then share to your personal pages. It's up to your social followers to decide whether to access it or not. The best way to get people engaged with your content is to make it good. Unhelpful or unprofessional content will hurt you more than help you. In promoting your content, remember to be relevant and not just talk about yourself and company. Don't be that person who ruins LinkedIn Groups with self-promotional spam.

2.    **Use social media to start relationships**. If you want to develop a relationship with a person or a company, a good place to start is to follow them on their social media accounts. Give to get. Rather than send an unsolicited sales pitch, try re-tweeting or sharing some of their content. Believe me, that will get you noticed by someone who is promoting content on social media. They will be much more likely to engage with you than the person who immediately goes for the kill with the spammy sales pitch. One of the biggest mistakes I see social sellers do is rush to move the sale ahead. They connect, and then they pitch their product or service. I don’t like it – and your prospects don’t like it. Instead, look for what’s in common, and have a conversation about that. Be a person and make a real connection.

3.    **Use social media to research and qualify prospects**. **The more focused you are in your sales and marketing efforts you are, the more successful you will be**. Rather than spray and pray, use social media to learn about your prospects and tailor your communications with them. If nothing else, view a prospect's LinkedIn profile and check out their website before you make any sales approach. LinkedIn’s ‘The State of Sales’ Reports shares…

- 77% of buyers saying that they wouldn’t engage with a salesperson if they didn’t do the necessary homework that would give them insights or knowledge into their business.

It's not rocket science, it's mostly common sense!

**If you view social selling as an immediate revenue generation tactic, you will invariably crash and burn. However, if you're helpful and respectful on social media, selling should come as a natural consequence to building a meaningful business relationship with people and businesses.**

**Thank you for taking the time out to read and share my latest article,**

**Joshua B Lee**

3-ways-men-can-help-close-gender-gap-jos.title: 3 Ways Men Can Help Close the Gender Gap
3-ways-men-can-help-close-gender-gap-jos.excerpt: I recently read an article on Entrepreneur about how the two female founders of Witchsy created a fake male co-founder to fight sexism(https://www.entrepreneur.com/article/299649). At the…
3-ways-men-can-help-close-gender-gap-jos.body:
I recently read an article on Entrepreneur about how the two female founders of Witchsy [created a fake male co-founder to fight sexism](https://www.entrepreneur.com/article/299649). At the same time I recently saw the World Economic Forum’s report on The [Global Gender Gap Report](http://www3.weforum.org/docs/GGGR16/WEF_Global_Gender_Gap_Report_2016.pdf) which found that the gender gap will not be closed for another 170 years. That means my great great great great granddaughter may get the same pay as a man in 2186. How can that be possible?

As the founder of Monstapreneur, my mission is to enable other entrepreneurs to find their distinct purpose and use that in a way that creates value. Not just personal value but economic value that is scalable and profitable. In my years working as an entrepreneur, I realized how many men I usually work with. Despite knowing many female entrepreneurs, it still seems difficult to connect with them but I know how crucial their diverse perspectives are to our success.

So what am I missing? What am I doing wrong that I’m not connecting with women in a way that can help bridge this terrible gender gap?

To answer some of my questions I chatted with [Rachel Braunstein](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rachelbraunstein/), a Partner Channel Marketing Manager at Microsoft who also created a community of women called [Rhea](https://www.facebook.com/RheaCommunity/). Rhea is a group of 'ladybosses that support each other to become more confident and find ways to work alongside men to create a more diverse and inclusive workforce'. Rachel’s perspectives from a corporate tech company and her passion for women, made me realize 3 things we need to do better to bridge the gender gap:

1)   Know when we have unconscious biases and do something to fight past it

Rachel spoke about many instances as a women in tech where the room was filled with men and where men have made inappropriate comments. From blowing kisses to assuming Rachel only wanted to speak about hair and makeup, many men have lacked the awareness and discipline to be respectful. I would hate for my daughter to experience this kind of sexism. As men we need to take a second and look around the room when women are outnumbered 10:1 and make an extra effort to make them feel welcome. Look at your invite lists to major events. Look at the amount of people your interviewing and hiring. Be honest with yourself and do something to include more women.

2)   Create safe zones for open discussions with her

There are many times when our boys club is underway, and as men we are talking about sports, beer and hunting says Rachel. Topics that many women can’t relate to. We need to make time for 1:1 lunches and smaller groups with men and women, so that we can find shared experiences together. Rachel mentioned that she understands that men can be worried about taking a female coworker, employee, or friend out, in fear that the meet up may be misconstrued. But she said to stop thinking about it, and we still need to do it. Don’t take the same girl out every time or create events like cooking or movies that both genders can relate to. Those safe zones are crucial for her to open up, feel more confident, and ultimately be successful.

3)   Celebrate her successes openly and frequently

Rachel said that the reality is many women are self-conscious and have a lot of self doubt. They do make decisions differently and at times have different fears and pressures than men do. When a manager can support her success and give her the confidence to progress in her career, the outcome can be huge. Men hold most of the powerful positions in corporate America especially when it comes to venture capital funding, so we need to support women in every way possible. Just saying great job or recommending her, can change the outcome for a woman’s entire life.

So what do you say guys, we have daughters, wives, mothers, and friends that are women in our lives and I want to hear your thoughts.

Thank you for taking the time and look forward to connecting with you more. Please click on any of the links to follow me on [Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/joshuablee/), [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/thejoshuablee/), [Twitter](https://twitter.com/thejoshuablee) and [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/thejoshuablee/)

Joshua B Lee

scale-1-10-where-you.title: On A Scale of 1 to 10, Where Are You?
scale-1-10-where-you.excerpt: A map is of no use if you can’t locate your current position on it. Taking stock of both your skill sets and your greatest hurdles is a vital step in mapping out your journey. Keeping an…
scale-1-10-where-you.body:
A map is of no use if you can’t locate your current position on it.

Taking stock of both your skill sets and your greatest hurdles is a vital step in mapping out your journey. Keeping an open mind is just as vital. Anticipating hurdles doesn’t necessitate a foreknowledge of them; it simply calls upon you to be resourceful and determined in your approach to overcoming them.

A poised mind and persistent spirit always create solutions by going over, under, around or through the obstacle, no matter the nature of it. Looking into the past is an exercise in gathering information, not seeking an old comfort zone to park in. This exercise makes sense only when your examined experiences provide lessons applicable to your life’s upward mobility.

When looking at your vision, health, relationships, and business, rate them weekly, or at least monthly, using a scale of 1 to 10. If your answer is not a confident 10, the new question becomes “Why not?” This is the point of “diving into the pain,” of acknowledging your current level of achievement…or lack thereof.

How do you mitigate that pain. The first step, however, is to acknowledge the pain so your subconscious mind knows there is a problem that not only needs, but also deserves, to be fixed. Start by using a personal journal. Write down your current ratings.

Most of us, especially men, are afraid to acknowledge pain. However, conscious individuals know the value of being honest with themselves. Doing so involves being able to acknowledge pain, regardless of circumstances. Women are traditionally more open and therefore tend to advance more fluidly through this part of the process. Regardless of your gender, this step is critical to living an elevated life.

2017-09-191205400-integratedlifeinspirat.title: Integrated Life Inspiration
2017-09-191205400-integratedlifeinspirat.excerpt: We were heading out to a Spurs game on December 5, 2008 when I heard the joyous and reality-altering news that I would be a father! Until then, I had been living large and mostly…
2017-09-191205400-integratedlifeinspirat.body:
We were heading out to a Spurs game on December 5, 2008 when I heard the joyous and reality-altering news that I would be a father!

Until then, I had been living large and mostly carefree—Vegas parties and all. I was at a high point in my career. To an outside observer, I appeared to be living the good life. Truth is I was rich on paper, poor in life. This was life’s second domino, warning me after the Playboy Club bet. However, this one gave me a deadline to get my overall life in order.

Unfortunately, I had also packed on pounds despite eating somewhat healthy. I knew drinking-while-partying was the culprit of the 32-pound “fireman’s torso weight suit” I was wearing 24/7. I was busy all the time and knew it was not a life to bring a child into. I was determined not to allow my business to be my “favorite child.” I was determined to spend time with my son and to have the energy to play and keep up with him.

I was an only child, so family—even a self-created sense of family—is very important to me. Before my son Jayden came along, my close friends had been my brothers and sisters. They still are. I also have half a dozen friends from elementary school whom I consider “family.” They can call me anytime day or night and I’ll be there for them. I have added others to this “family” along the way. Still, at times I was giving more than I was receiving, and it caused cash-flow problems.

The online advertising crash of 2008, coupled with my tendency to support people through their tough times, nearly cratered my business. There was more going out than coming in each month. Instead of making tough decisions and cuts to weather the economic storm, I burned through all the company savings. Then I compounded my mistake by also burning through all my personal savings in an attempt to keep the company operating in an economic environment that no longer existed. Stress and a mountain of other issues were crushing me.

This is when I started thinking about the people and activities in my life from an energy standpoint. Did this person or activity bring my energy up? Or, did it bring my energy down? When only one side is giving on a continual basis, it drains energy and profitability. In contrast, when both sides are committed to the mutual achievement of goals, energy and profitability increase exponentially. Learning this, albeit the hard way, was a big aha moment for me.

I focused on my health and developed what would become the health pillar of the Integrated Life Formula. I began spending more time with mutual energy creators, which left no time for “energy vampires.” I have now attracted a fantastic group of friends and business mentors who I am 100 percent certain I could call on to be there for me just as I would be for them.

The impending arrival of my son motivated me to action on all fronts. I became much more serious about taking the necessary steps in my life to have overall prosperity, not just business and financial prosperity. I started thinking about where I wanted my life to go. This got me thinking about deep topics such as my life’s vision and the spiritual aspects that provided its undercurrent of meaning. So many times in my life, I had felt like an observer, watching my own life as one watches a movie. I wanted to be driving the car that was my life instead of standing on the curb watching someone else in the driver’s seat, passing me by in my car!

With fewer than nine months to go, I immediately set about building my team and processes to unshackle me from my business. I had resolved that I was going to spend the first six months of my son’s life on sabbatical, completely devoted to him.

I kept my promise to myself and learned valuable and unforeseen lessons, both gratifying and unsettling, in the process. I am thankful to my team and advisers for keeping our multimillion-dollar business running during the six months I was away.

It had been running, but it had not been running on all cylinders. I thought I had put excellent systems and a top-notch team into place. However, once I got actively involved in my business again, I realized my perception had not been reality. Fortunately, I was able to reassess my previous judgments and processes, and repair and rebuild from a platform of enlightened understanding.

These events and experiences were the building blocks that would become the Integrated Life Formula I use in my own life. I have always felt a calling to be a mentor to others. I realized how much advice and help I had given to so many companies in the online advertising space because I believe we live in a world of abundance. Many of these companies were potential competitors, but I saw something in them. I gave a ton of my time and even tested their technology to help them get off the ground.

Once I created and lived this system, I wanted to help others. I am passionate about coaching other entrepreneurs on how to put this system to use in their lives. You can’t get to freedom without a lot of hard work in the beginning—unless you win the lottery or are a trust-fund baby. This is why the Integrated Life Formula is so important for reaching your elevated life of freedom.

Interested in learning more about the Integrated Life Formula schedule a 15 min call with me and lets connect here - > http://bit.ly/2y5HFrp

whats-first-thing-you-do-morning.title: What's the First Thing You do in the Morning?
whats-first-thing-you-do-morning.excerpt: When I set out to help my clients, the first thing I ask is “What do you truly want to accomplish?” To get a fuller understanding of this, I start by inquiring about their morning ritual.…
whats-first-thing-you-do-morning.body:
When I set out to help my clients, the first thing I ask is “What do you truly want to accomplish?” To get a fuller understanding of this, I start by inquiring about their morning ritual. “What is the first thing you do when you wake up in the morning?” In terms of mapping a strategy to wealth, this may seem like an obtuse question, yet its answer can set immeasurable precedents for the rest of your life.

Most people say they reach for their cell phone. Bingo! One seemingly innocuous reply, yet I now know that outside factors take precedence over designing their own life happiness and fulfillment. Would you answer the same? If so, the most important pieces of your life — your personal mission, health, relationships, and business — are taking a back seat to a technological device. Your interaction with a thing has become more important than your interaction with your life. This robs you (and the world) on many levels. If you don’t protect these precious treasures, external parties will be more than happy to stake their claim to your territory. The inevitable outcome of not commanding the Integrated Life Formula of your life is despair, general unhappiness, or, at the very best, that gnawing feeling of “Is this all there is?”

No one else knows your inner desires better than you, no outside party can know your Why better than you, and no one else knows the intrinsic motivators that will inspire you to charge through the inevitable setbacks you will face in life. Ultimately, regardless of the persuasion of external forces, you can always trace the choices that dictate the direction and momentum of your life back to intrinsic motivators. Best to spend time getting to know them… and nurturing them.

Your morning ritual is critical to setting up your day for success. If you have yet to find the success you’re looking for, upgrading your morning ritual will be a key driver to changing your behavior and achieving the goals you seek.

importance-community.title: The Importance Of Community
importance-community.excerpt: Have you ever attended an event or conference and been bored out of your mind? Ever signed up for a “mastermind” or other exclusive gathering which promises to completely change your life…
importance-community.body:
Have you ever attended an event or conference and been bored out of your mind?

Ever signed up for a “mastermind” or other exclusive gathering which promises to completely change your life and dump piles of cash at your feet?

Are you tired of walking away from events such as these with a notebook or file on your laptop full of ideas that sits completely ignored as you get “back to reality”?

If you answered yes to to any of these questions then read on because I have a few hard truths to share with you.

Truths about the difference between attending an event and achieving your goals.

And why immersing yourself in the RIGHT community is so important.

We’ve heard it all before…

The first thing they try to pull you in with is an “all star” speaker lineup. Then you’re hit with a promise of exclusive content…

And it’s all tied together with a nice bow of fancy food and a snazzy place to stay.

While enticements of this nature are glamorous they don’t really help you in your personal or professional life.

The reality is there are very few gatherings that live up to all the hype.

But I found one and wanted to take just a minute to tell you why I’m so attracted to it. It’s called [Baby Bath Water](http://www.babybathwaterinstitute.com/).

Weird name, incredible experience.

Why? Because the founders [Michael Lovitch](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lovitch/) and [Hollis Carter](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hollis-carter-9103195/) are on a mission. That mission is simple.

Be the best version of YOU, that you can be.

Which means there aren’t any people slinging business cards or asking “what do you do for a living?”.

It’s simply a place for entrepreneurs, business owners, and creators to come together to share their knowledge.

Community members own or are involved with business across the spectrum. Their experiences give birth to a environment that allows you to choose your own adventure.

At [Baby Bath Water](http://www.babybathwaterinstitute.com/) events, you are completely free to do as you choose:

- Participate in a workshop with the faculty

- Get involved in one of the panels

- Enjoy the outdoors

- Join your new friends for a drink or three

- Eat your face off with healthy, home-cooked, delicious food

- Dance all night to live music

Never get pitched! All [Baby Bathwater](http://www.babybathwaterinstitute.com/) events are “No Pitch Zones”.

### This means no pitching from the staff or members so everyone can be fully present and exchange REAL value.

### If you want to go skiing, hiking, climbing, mountain biking or just sit in the hot tub and talk to other members you can. There’s no pressure to sit in a room all day furiously jotting down notes.

No FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out). Just a bunch of highly vetted incredible people coming together to share their personal and professional knowledge.

A true community.

Now for those of you who are more analytical by nature… you may be thinking something along the lines of “that sounds awesome! But what’s the real ROI on something like that?”.

I get it. We all want to succeed and achieve our goals. As Beachbody SVP and founder of Round Two Partners [Babak Azad](https://www.facebook.com/babakazadpublic/) says:

“My sense is that the relationships I'm building here, whether it's the people here or people they know, is going to lead to something. Otherwise, I wouldn't come back.”

But you don’t have to take his word for it.

Baby Bath Water has a slew of testimonials from members who swear by the value of the community.

They understand the NEED for a truly unique experience which facilitates personal and professional growth.

[Ryan Levesque](https://www.facebook.com/askryanlevesque/), best selling author of ASK and creator of the ASK METHOD says this about Baby Bath Water:

“It was just magic. It was an experience that I’ll remember for the rest of my life. Everybody here has this tremendous sense of contribution.”

I could go on and on but at this point I think the message is clear.

If you’re not already involved in an incredible community stop what you’re doing and make that a priority.

I highly recommend [Baby Bath Water](http://www.babybathwaterinstitute.com/). But even if you don’t think it’s a good fit for you… take the time to find a community that helps you achieve your goals. A base of people who want to help you grow.

Your future depends on it.

persistence-simple-key-results.title: Forget overnight success
persistence-simple-key-results.excerpt: Remember last week how we talked about overcoming your fear? If you missed the article you can find it here:…
persistence-simple-key-results.body:
Remember last week how we talked about overcoming your fear?

If you missed the article you can find it here:

[https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/three-key-steps-overcome-fear-joshua-b-lee](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/three-key-steps-overcome-fear-joshua-b-lee)

So many of you may be asking, ok now what?

Iʼm fearless, I know how to make my message more authentic, I have found my voice, and I am clear on my target audience.

What do I do with all of this fantastic information?

Will all of this actually help my business?

 I will say this...

You will not get results overnight. You are in this for the long haul. It can sometimes take years to build the business you are envisioning in your head. Stay focused. Celebrate the short term goals but at the same time do not get complacent and do not give up.

If you are truly not operating from a place of fear you will not be afraid to succeed and you will not be afraid to fail.

The one thing that you need to focus on is persistence. Even when you feel like you have everything in place and it seems like you are still getting nowhere. You continue to write articles, you continue to put out content even if it seems like you are hitting a dead end with all of it.

The truth is your audience is probably reading your content. However, if you have only put out three articles, people are less likely to see you and your business as an authority in comparison to a business who has put out 300 articles. Your audience is more willing to trust someone who has been in the game for some period of time.

So be patient.

Put the time in.

After a while it just becomes a numbers game. Once you have put enough high quality content out there your audience will start to take notice.

You will start gaining clients, credibility, and start developing a decent success rate. Your business success will begin to snowball. Word will begin to spread and clients, success with those clients, testimonials, and more clients with it.

 So no this is not a get rich quick scheme.

Put in the hard work, put in the time in the beginning stages, and you will earn the position you’ve been gunning for.

You wonʼt have to work hard forever. But when building the foundation, the drive, consistency, and patience are the most important factors. This is when you need to be the most confident in your message because chances are, in the beginning, others will not share that same confidence.

 Everyone wants to see results.

 So be confident.

Until then practicing that confidence is so key, because you need to be readywhen your audience decides to engage with what you are trying to give them.
